title_en: Bishops lament White House meeting that produced photo with Trump
title_zh: 主教们对白宫会议与特朗普合影表示遗憾
summary: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Trump.
summary_zh: 两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议制作了一张公开分发的他们与总统一起祈祷的照片。
body_en: Bishops lament White House meeting that produced photo with Trump, say session was "manipulated" and "exploited" - CBS News
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Trump.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, in a statement titled "A Public Apology," said Sunday that he had received many questions and comments — some of them distraught — about the meeting on Thursday that he and 11 other bishops attended.
He said the meeting was speedily publicized by the White House with photos and a video without consent of the participants, less than two weeks away from the midterm elections .

"I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way," Grob said.
The bishop of Des Moines, Iowa, William Joensen, also issued a statement making clear he felt the White House had taken advantage of the bishops.

"I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose," he wrote. "I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels."

Asked whether the White House had received the bishops' consent for releasing the photos and video, the press office declined to answer. Instead, White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers replied, "There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it."

The White House invitation to the bishops, extended in September, offered discussion about such issues as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas, abortion and the use of federal tax credits to support private education, according to Joensen and Grob.

"The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party," wrote Grob. "We were told the meeting was to be a private discussion, that several Catholic members of the Cabinet might make an appearance, and that there could be an opportunity to pray privately with the president."
"It did not take long thereafter for the White House to post a video and photos of the prayer," Grob said.

"I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election," he added. "I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family had been harmed by the president's policies.

" ... We came in good faith to try to work for the betterment of our fellow human beings, to ease their suffering, to build up the common good, and to pray with a president, not to pose for a political photo opportunity to benefit the few. We should never have been put in that position by the White House.

"I did not go without reservations. I wish I had heeded them," Grob concluded. "Please know that I have heard these concerns, understand how I caused them, and I apologize for any damage my actions have done."

Collectively, members of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops have diverse views on Mr. Trump and his administration's policies. Minnesota-based Bishop Robert Barron, for example, agreed to serve on his Religious Liberty Commission, which was filled almost entirely with conservative Christians. Some other bishops vehemently denounced aspects of Mr. Trump's tough stance on immigration enforcement, saying it runs counter to Catholic teaching.
body_zh: 主教们对与特朗普合影的白宫会议表示遗憾，称会议被“操纵”和“利用” - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
两位天主教主教对同意举行一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与特朗普总统祈祷的照片。
密尔沃基大主教杰弗里·格罗布周日在一份题为“公开道歉”的声明中表示，他收到了许多关于他和其他 11 名主教周四参加的会议的问题和评论，其中一些令人心烦意乱。
他说，距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间，白宫在未经与会者同意的情况下迅速用照片和视频公开了这次会议。
格罗布说：“我感到非常悲伤，不仅因为我造成的痛苦，还因为对一群宗教领袖来说如此神圣的事情，即向我们的天父祈祷，会被以这种方式操纵。”
爱荷华州得梅因主教威廉·约恩森也发表声明，明确表示他认为白宫利用了主教们的利益。
他写道：“我希望自己能更精明一些，不要那么简单，就像那些利用我们的会议来达到党派政治目的的人一样。” “我祈祷我今后能更加谨慎和明智，尽管我仍然坚定地开放地参与各级政治领导人并为他们祈祷。”
当被问及白宫是否已获得主教同意发布这些照片和视频时，新闻办公室拒绝回答。相反，白宫发言人泰勒·罗杰斯回答说：“对于美国天主教徒来说，从来没有比特朗普总统更伟大的总统，他的出色记录证明了这一点。”
乔恩森和格罗布表示，白宫于九月份向主教发出了邀请，邀请他们就移民执法、宗教工作者签证、堕胎以及利用联邦税收抵免支持私立教育等问题进行讨论。
格罗布写道：“这次会议绝不是对总统、他的政策或他的政党的认可。” “我们被告知这次会议将是一次私人讨论，几位天主教内阁成员可能会出席，并且可能有机会与总统私下祈祷。”
格罗布说：“不久之后，白宫就发布了祈祷的视频和照片。”
他补充说：“我很快就开始收到严重关切的信息，担心我在全国大选前不到两周的时间里无意中参与了一场政治活动。” “我还听到一些人因为总统政策对他们或他们的家人造成的伤害而感到受伤。
“......我们真诚地来到这里，努力为我们的人类同胞谋福利，减轻他们的痛苦，建立共同利益，并与总统一起祈祷，而不是摆出政治拍照机会来造福少数人。白宫不应该把我们置于这样的境地。”
“我并不是毫无保留地去的。我希望我当时听从了他们的意见，”格罗布总结道。 “请知道我已经听到了这些担忧，理解我是如何造成这些担忧的，我为我的行为造成的任何损害道歉。”
总的来说，美国天主教主教会议的成员对特朗普及其政府的政策有不同的看法。例如，明尼苏达州的罗伯特·巴伦主教同意在他的宗教自由委员会任职，该委员会几乎全部都是保守派基督徒。其他一些主教强烈谴责特朗普在移民执法问题上的强硬立场，称这与天主教教义背道而驰。

title_en: Trump intensifies anti-Muslim rhetoric against Abdul El-Sayed at Michigan rally – US politics live

summary_zh: 美国总统因质疑参议员候选人对国家忠诚度的言论而受到谴责 美国中期选举是什么以及为什么要举行
body_en: Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security.

The president also questioned his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally. Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a “jihadist” who was “on the side of the terrorists” and would “have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate.”

He also repeatedly invoked 9/11, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93, AP reported.
El-Sayed, who would become the nation’s first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country “shameful” and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups.

The Republican president’s remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president’s outreach to Arab American voters in 2024. “The president’s statements are out of line,” he said in a phone interview. “They are crossing a red line. They are racist.”

Trump also reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums and encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind. The comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end.

Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.”
“You are a great athlete,” Trump also said to Husted. “Congratulations.” Trump was speaking at the rally to support Mike Rogers, the Michigan Republican Senate candidate.
Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan

Mary Peltola , a Democrat who is running for Alaska ’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said. The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.

Todd Blanche, Donald Trump’s attorney general, lashed out during an interview on Sunday while defending the justice department’s pre-emptive lawsuit to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate results if the GOP incumbent loses, calling a TV host’s question “crazy”. The testy repartee unfolded on CNN’s State of the Union over the DoJ’s unprecedented legal action, which alleges that there could be “voter confusion” due to two candidates named Dan Sullivan on Alaska’s ballot. Trump told reporters, “I’m the one that said do it” when asked about the suit.

The US military has given Elon Musk’s SpaceX access to restricted space tracking data, raising a new round of questions about whether the Trump administration is attempting to hand over traffic control in Earth’s orbit to a controversial donor. The access also raises new national security questions, industry observers say.

Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) has decreased significantly over the past year in the US following restrictions imposed by the Trump administration , which has forced more people to seek help from food banks or go hungry, stakeholders say. The number of people who receive food stamps has dropped from 41.6 million in July 2025, before the One Big Beautiful Act took effect, to 36.5 million in June 2026, a 13% decrease, according to the latest data from the US Department of Agriculture , which administers the program.
body_zh: 您好，欢迎来到美国政治直播博客。
唐纳德·特朗普周日强化了针对密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的反穆斯林言论，将他描绘成对国家安全的威胁。
总统还质疑他对美国的忠诚度，言论遭到一位前阿拉伯裔美国盟友的严厉谴责。特朗普称前底特律卫生官员埃尔赛义德是“圣战分子”，“站在恐怖分子一边”，“在获准进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器”。
据美联社报道，他还多次援引 9/11 事件，将阻止埃尔赛义德进入参议院会议厅与联合航空 93 号航班上的劫机者进行反击的乘客进行比较。
如果当选，埃尔赛义德将成为该国第一位穆斯林参议员，他称针对他对国家忠诚的攻击是“可耻的”，并一再否认与极端主义团体有任何联系。
这位共和党总统的言论遭到了特朗普阿拉伯裔美国人组织创始人比沙拉·巴巴的谴责，该组织曾帮助领导总统在2024年向阿拉伯裔美国选民进行宣传。“总统的言论不合时宜，”他在电话采访中表示。 “他们正在跨越红线。他们是种族主义者。”
特朗普还重申了他对丰满臀部的喜爱，并鼓励观众称赞说唱歌手妮琪·米娜的臀部。关于米纳臀部的评论是在他解释他最近对俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德臀部的观察时发表的。
十月初，特朗普谈到这位前大学橄榄球运动员时说：“我不经常对男人这样做。我开始检查他的身体，因为我不知道他是一名伟大的运动员。我上下观察。我看着他的屁股，我看着整个——然后我看着他的手。看看他的手。他有这些，就像爪子。”
“你是一位伟大的运动员，”特朗普还对赫斯特德说。 “恭喜。”特朗普在支持密歇根州共和党参议员候选人迈克·罗杰斯的集会上发表讲话。
特朗普在密歇根州为迈克·罗杰斯和妮琪·米娜的臀部集会
竞选阿拉斯加唯一美国参议院席位的民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）的竞选团队表示，她和她的家人在周六开车前往竞选站点时遭遇车祸，受了轻伤。佩尔托拉的竞选团队在周日的一份声明中表示，当时一家人正在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会年度宴会的途中，另一辆车撞上了载着佩尔托拉及其家人的车辆。碰撞后佩尔托拉需要医疗救助。

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)的司法部长托德·布兰奇(Todd Blanche)在周日接受采访时猛烈抨击，同时为司法部的先发制人诉讼进行辩护，如果共和党现任议员败选，该诉讼将阻止阿拉斯加州美国参议院结果的认证，称电视主持人的问题“疯狂”。美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的国情咨文节目对美国司法部前所未有的法律行动展开了激烈的对答，该行动声称，阿拉斯加选票上两名名为丹·沙利文的候选人可能会造成“选民混乱”。当被问及这套诉讼时，特朗普告诉记者，“我是那个说这么做的人”。
美国军方已允许埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 访问受限的太空跟踪数据，引发了新一轮的质疑：特朗普政府是否试图将地球轨道上的交通控制权移交给有争议的捐助者。行业观察人士表示，这种访问还引发了新的国家安全问题。
利益相关者表示，在特朗普政府施加限制后，过去一年美国补充营养援助计划 (Snap) 的注册人数大幅减少，迫使更多人向食品银行寻求帮助，否则就会挨饿。根据管理该计划的美国农业部的最新数据，领取食品券的人数已从“美丽大法案”生效前的 2025 年 7 月的 4160 万人下降到 2026 年 6 月的 3650 万人，下降了 13%。

summary_zh: 特朗普总统的和平委员会任命了雪莉·格林斯潘（Shelley Greenspan），她在拜登执政期间担任白宫犹太社区联络人
body_en: President Trump's Board of Peace has appointed Shelley Greenspan, who served as the White House's Jewish community liaison during the Biden administration, to lead its outreach to Congress and the Washington think tank community.

Why it matters: Greenspan's selection is part of an effort by the Board of Peace to increase bipartisan support for President Trump's Gaza peace plan. The implementation of the plan is expected to get a renewed push after the midterms and the formation of a new Israeli government.
The possibility of Democrats controlling the House or Senate makes the need for bipartisanship on the Gaza plan even more crucial.
Driving the news: The plan has been stuck due to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to take any steps in Gaza before the October 27 elections.
In recent months, multiple prominent Democrats have expressed support for Trump's plan. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton endorsed the plan in June, calling it the most viable proposal.

Zoom in: Greenspan, a career civil servant at the State Department, was at the White House National Security Council during Biden's term — both as the American Jewish community liaison and the director for partnerships and elobal engagement.
At the Board of Peace she will lead external affairs, putting her in charge of outreach to Congress and Middle East experts.

What they're saying: "Shelley brings deep experience working across the aisle, having earned the trust of Democrats and Republicans alike through her service at the White House, National Security Council, and State Department in Democratic and Republican administrations," the Board of Peace told Axios in a statement.
"Sustained, bipartisan support from Congress is essential to the work ahead, and Shelley is uniquely capable of leading this effort," the board added.
Greenspan told Axios in a statement that she worked in her last State Department role to advance Trump's "vision for peace and prosperity in the Middle East."
"I saw how the President's 20-Point Plan can tangibly deliver for the peoples of Gaza and Israel. I look forward to continuing that work with the Board," she said.
body_zh: 特朗普总统的和平委员会已任命在拜登政府期间担任白宫犹太社区联络员的雪莱·格林斯潘领导和平委员会与国会和华盛顿智库社区的联系。
为什么重要：格林斯潘的选择是和平委员会为增加两党对特朗普总统加沙和平计划的支持而做出的努力的一部分。预计该计划的实施将在中期选举和以色列新政府组建后得到新的推动。
民主党控制众议院或参议院的可能性使得加沙计划上两党合作的必要性变得更加重要。
最新消息：由于以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡拒绝在 10 月 27 日选举之前在加沙采取任何措施，该计划陷入停滞。
近几个月来，多名民主党知名人士表达了对特朗普计划的支持。前国务卿希拉里·克林顿 (Hillary Clinton) 在六月认可了该计划，称其为最可行的建议。
放大：格林斯潘是国务院的职业公务员，在拜登任期内担任白宫国家安全委员会成员，既担任美国犹太社区联络人，又担任合作伙伴关系和内部交往主任。
在和平委员会，她将领导对外事务，负责与国会和中东专家的联系。
他们的说法：和平委员会在一份声明中告诉 Axios，“雪莱带来了跨党派工作的丰富经验，通过她在白宫、国家安全委员会以及国务院在民主党和共和党政府中的服务，赢得了民主党和共和党的信任。”
董事会补充说：“国会的持续、两党支持对于未来的工作至关重要，而雪莱具有领导这项工作的独特能力。”
格林斯潘在一份声明中告诉 Axios，她在国务院的最后一个职务是为了推进特朗普的“中东和平与繁荣愿景”。
“我看到了总统的 20 点计划如何切实为加沙和以色列人民带来好处。我期待着与委员会继续开展这项工作，”她说。

body_en: Discontent with Trump buoys Democrats in Ohio: ‘People are disgusted by the corruption’
In a reliably red state, candidates say dissatisfied voters tell them they’re planning to vote Democrat for the first time
Democrat Kim McCarthy is canvassing in a middle-class Ohio neighborhood of four-bedroom, three-bathroom homes. There are $70,000 trucks in the driveways and robot lawnmowers at work.
“This is a neighborhood of two incomes and young families; people working hard,” says McCarthy, who is running against a three-time Republican incumbent for a seat in Ohio’s house of representatives.

Despite the manicured lawns, these are the very Ohioans struggling from the fallout of many of the Trump administration’s policies. They live in a district that includes the largest single-site employer in Ohio – the Wright-Patterson air force base – whose civilian contractors and employees have been hit hard by federal workforce cuts . Rising mortgage interest rates and wider affordability concerns are top of mind for many.

McCarthy’s opponent, Brian Lampton, beat her in a previous election by 15 points. In the presidential election two years ago, Trump won 60% of the vote here in Fairborn. But having knocked on thousands of Greene county doors, she says she’s noticed something different this year: people are telling her on the doorstep that they are planning to vote Democrat down the ballot for the first time.
“One woman I was speaking to earlier who worked in the military and recently retired was like: ‘Oh my God, I can’t afford anything.’ You could kind of see the sadness in her eyes,” she says.
This month, candidates from both parties running for office were invited to a forum held by the Greene County Tea Party , a conservative group, which McCarthy attended.

Of only two residents to open their doors to McCarthy in the presence of a Guardian reporter, one said she and her husband had already voted Democrat down the ballot, while the other thanked her and said they would look into her policies.

For more than a decade, Ohio has been considered a firm Republican stronghold, but after 20 months of extreme Trump administration policies, signs of discontent with the status quo are appearing here. That could be critical for Democrats at every level on the ballot – the party is trying to reclaim a US Senate seat, the governor’s mansion, and a host of competitive house seats around the state.
Early voting indicators in Ohio suggest that participation among affiliated Democrats is higher this year when compared to 2024, especially in predominantly Republican districts.

According to the Ohio secretary of state’s data portal website , by 13 October more early voting ballots were returned in rural Defiance county by Democratic affiliated voters than by Republicans, despite Trump winning 69% of the vote in the county in the 2024 presidential election.
The county also had the highest ballot return rate in the state, at 19%, suggesting a high level of motivation.

T he economy isn’t the only thing on voters’ minds. “The number one issue in Defiance right now is the proposed datacenter . There is a local investor who is entertaining the idea of selling property to a datacenter investor,” says Rebecca Kirkland of the Defiance County Democratic Party.

Trump has repeatedly encouraged communities to accept datacenters, telling supporters at a campaign rally outside Dayton, on 3 October, “We want them,” despite broad bipartisan opposition to their presence.

Home to a General Motors powertrain foundry that employs more than 500 people, Defiance county has also been hit hard by Trump’s tariffs war on Canada: among the plant’s main customers is the GM-owned St Catharines engine plant in Ontario, with engine parts that are built in Defiance are shipped for assembly across the Canadian border.
“There aren’t many high-paying jobs available in this area. We see posts on community Facebook pages of people looking for assistance finding work, housing or financial assistance,” says Kirkland.

Still, in a state that for decades turned older and whiter and was won by Trump in the last three presidential elections, Democrats know the odds are stacked against them. And pollsters are cautioning that the surge in early voting might not indicate that more Ohioans will vote for Democrats by the end of the election.

“I suspect any surge we may be seeing among Democrats could be due to concerns they may have about the USPS given the negative signaling by Donald Trump about the sanctity of mail-in votes,” says Robert Alexander, a professor of political science at Bowling Green State University.
“Many have grown untrustworthy of the administration and would prefer to cast their ballots in person rather than take any risks sending it through the post office.”
body_zh: 对特朗普的不满鼓舞了俄亥俄州的民主党人：“人们对腐败感到厌恶”
在一个可靠的红色州，候选人表示，不满意的选民告诉他们，他们计划第一次投票给民主党
民主党人金·麦卡锡 (Kim McCarthy) 正在俄亥俄州的一个中产阶级社区拉票，那里有四间卧室、三间浴室的房屋。车道上停着价值 70,000 美元的卡车，割草机器人正在工作。
“这是一个有两种收入和年轻家庭的社区；人们努力工作，”麦卡锡说，他正在与一位三届共和党议员竞选俄亥俄州众议院席位。
尽管草坪修剪整齐，但这些正是在特朗普政府许多政策的影响下挣扎的俄亥俄人。他们居住的地区包括俄亥俄州最大的单一地点雇主——赖特-帕特森空军基地——该基地的民用承包商和雇员受到联邦劳动力削减的严重打击。抵押贷款利率上升和更广泛的负担能力担忧是许多人最关心的问题。
麦卡锡的对手布莱恩·兰普顿(Brian Lampton)在之前的选举中以15个百分点的优势击败了她。在两年前的总统选举中，特朗普在费尔伯恩这里赢得了60%的选票。但在敲开了格林县数千户人家的门后，她说今年她注意到了一些不同的情况：人们在门口告诉她，他们计划第一次投票给民主党。
“我之前与一位在军队工作、最近退休的女性交谈过，她说：‘天哪，我买不起任何东西。’你可以看到她眼中的悲伤，”她说。
本月，竞选公职的两党候选人均受邀参加保守派团体格林县茶党举办的论坛，麦卡锡也参加了该论坛。
只有两名居民在卫报记者在场的情况下向麦卡锡敞开大门，其中一名居民表示，她和她的丈夫已经投票否决了民主党，而另一名居民则对她表示感谢，并表示他们将调查她的政策。
十多年来，俄亥俄州一直被认为是共和党的坚固据点，但经过特朗普政府20个月的极端政策，这里出现了对现状不满的迹象。这对于各个级别的民主党人来说都至关重要——该党正试图夺回美国参议院席位、州长官邸以及全州一系列有竞争力的众议院席位。
俄亥俄州的早期投票指标表明，与 2024 年相比，今年附属民主党人的参与度更高，尤其是在共和党占主导地位的选区。
根据俄亥俄州务卿数据门户网站的数据，截至 10 月 13 日，尽管特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中赢得了迪法恩斯县农村地区 69% 的选票，但截至 10 月 13 日，民主党附属选民在迪法恩斯县寄出的提前投票选票多于共和党选民。
该县的选票回报率也是全州最高的，达到 19%，这表明该县的积极性很高。
经济并不是选民唯一关心的问题。 “迪法恩斯目前的首要问题是拟议的数据中心。有一位当地投资者正在考虑将财产出售给数据中心投资者，”迪法恩斯县民主党的丽贝卡·柯克兰 (Rebecca Kirkland) 说道。
特朗普一再鼓励社区接受数据中心，并在 10 月 3 日代顿郊外的竞选集会上对支持者说，“我们想要它们”，尽管两党普遍反对数据中心的存在。
迪法恩斯县是一家拥有 500 多名员工的通用汽车动力总成铸造厂的所在地，也受到了特朗普对加拿大关税战的沉重打击：该工厂的主要客户之一是通用汽车旗下的安大略省圣凯瑟琳斯发动机工厂，在迪法恩斯制造的发动机零件被运往加拿大边境进行组装。
“这个地区没有太多高薪工作。我们在社区 Facebook 页面上看到人们寻求工作、住房或经济援助的帖子，”柯克兰说。
尽管如此，在一个几十年来变得越来越老、越来越白、并且在过去三届总统选举中由特朗普获胜的州，民主党人知道他们的胜算不大。民意调查机构警告说，提前投票的激增可能并不表明更多的俄亥俄州人会在选举结束时投票给民主党。
鲍林格林州立大学政治学教授罗伯特·亚历山大表示：“我怀疑民主党人中可能看到的任何激增可能是由于他们对美国邮政局的担忧，因为唐纳德·特朗普对邮寄选票的神圣性发出了负面信号。”
“许多人已经不再信任政府，宁愿亲自投票，也不愿冒任何风险通过邮局寄出选票。”

summary_zh: 美国中期选举临近，我们通过数据来了解特朗普领导下的美国经济真实情况。
body_en: ‘We don’t have inflation’? Five charts show the US economic reality of Trump’s second term so far | US midterm elections 2026
‘We don’t have inflation’? Five charts show the US economic reality of Trump’s second term so far
As the US midterm elections approach, we take a look at data to see a true picture of the US economy under Trump
With the midterm elections fast approaching, many Americans have the economy on their minds.

US voters are exhausted by years of higher prices. Donald Trump won the presidency in 2024 on promises to lower inflation and undo the damage he said the Biden administration had inflicted on the economy.
Too little, too late: Trump takes on gas prices as fuel costs hamper his midterm hopes

In Trump’s view, his plan is working. At a recent rally in Montana, Trump boasted about the current economy, framing it as a booming time for Americans. “We’re richer now,” he said. “We don’t have inflation.”

Economic data paints a different picture. Inflation , especially gas prices, have soared over the last year. The job market has been in stasis, and higher interest rates have meant it’s more expensive for Americans to borrow money for loans and mortgages.

These fluctuations have a concrete impact on the lives of Americans. A recent Harris poll for the Guardian found that a majority of Americans, including some Republicans, disagree. Nearly two-thirds said they believe the country is experiencing a recession, and many said higher prices have been a pain point. Americans are reporting having trouble saving, and a third polled said one surprise bill could sink them financially.
Here’s what the data shows us about Trump’s second term so far.

The rate of price increases has dramatically cooled since its peak in 2022, when the pandemic’s economic stimulus packages found their way into consumer prices. Inflation peaked at 9.1%, a 40-year high, in June 2022.
In January 2025, the month when Trump started his second term, inflation was down to 3%. By April 2025, it would be 2.3% – the lowest rate since 2021.

That’s when things start to get bumpy. After Trump placed tariffs on nearly everything that the US imports, inflation started to heat up again, climbing back up to 3% in September 2025. After many of his tariffs were paused and eventually found to be illegal, prices started going down again. In January and February 2026, inflation was back down to 2.4%.
The Iran war, specifically its impact on oil prices, has brought inflation back up to levels not seen since 2023. In May, inflation reached 4.2% and has hovered above 3.4% since.

It’s been nearly six years since Americans has seen inflation at a manageable 2% level. Price increases build up over time and can put a squeeze on budgets, which is why it’s such a sensitive point for voters during a crucial election.
In the Guardian’s recent poll with the Harris Poll, gas prices were the most common pain point for Americans, with 83% saying they’re making a dent in their current finances.
A line chart showing average gas prices in the US

Soon after the war in Iran began, the strait of Hormuz, a key route that a fifth of the world’s oil typically passes through, was blocked off. Its closure has pushed up prices all around the world. Though the US itself is a major oil producer, prices have still surged since the war. The average price of gas was $4.32 per gallon in mid-October, according to AAA, nearly $1.30 a gallon higher than a year ago.

Even for an oil-producing state like Texas, a gallon of gas is $3.81 compared with $2.64 a year ago. Meanwhile, drivers in California, a state that imports much of its gas from overseas, are paying $6.21 per gallon.

The labor market is another metric used to measure the health of the economy, and while the US job market has seen some growth since Trump took office again, figures have fluctuated over the last year. In 2025, altogether 181,000 new jobs were added to the economy, compared with 2.2m jobs in 2024.
body_zh: “我们没有通货膨胀”？五张图表显示特朗普第二任期迄今的美国经济现实2026 年美国中期选举
“我们没有通货膨胀”？五张图表显示特朗普第二任期迄今为止的美国经济现实
美国中期选举临近，我们通过数据看特朗普治下的美国经济真实面貌
随着中期选举的临近，许多美国人都关心经济问题。
US voters are exhausted by years of higher prices.唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 因承诺降低通胀并消除他所说的拜登政府对经济造成的损害而赢得了 2024 年总统职位。
太少，太晚：特朗普对汽油价格的反应是因为燃料成本阻碍了他的中期希望
In Trump’s view, his plan is working.最近在蒙大拿州的一次集会上，特朗普吹嘘当前的经济，将其描述为美国人的繁荣时期。 “We’re richer now,” he said. “We don’t have inflation.”
经济数据描绘了一幅不同的图景。去年，通货膨胀，尤其是天然气价格飙升。就业市场一直处于停滞状态，利率上升意味着美国人借贷和抵押贷款的成本更高。
这些波动对美国人的生活产生了具体影响。 《卫报》最近进行的哈里斯民意调查发现，包括一些共和党人在内的大多数美国人不同意这一观点。近三分之二的人表示他们认为该国正在经历经济衰退，许多人表示价格上涨一直是一个痛点。美国人报告说他们在储蓄方面遇到了困难，三分之一的受访者表示，一项意外的法案可能会让他们陷入财务困境。
以下是数据向我们展示的有关特朗普第二任期迄今为止的情况。
自2022年的峰值以来，价格上涨的速度已急剧降温，当时大流行的经济刺激计划影响了消费者价格。 2022 年 6 月，通胀率达到 9.1% 的峰值，创 40 年来新高。
2025 年 1 月，即特朗普开始第二任期的月份，通货膨胀率降至 3%。到 2025 年 4 月，这一数字将达到 2.3%，这是 2021 年以来的最低水平。
那就是事情开始变得坎坷的时候。在特朗普对几乎所有美国进口商品征收关税后，通胀开始再次升温，并于 2025 年 9 月回升至 3%。在他的许多关税被暂停并最终被发现非法后，价格再次开始下跌。 2026 年 1 月和 2 月，通胀率回落至 2.4%。
伊朗战争，特别是其对油价的影响，使通货膨胀率回升至2023年以来的最高水平。5月份，通货膨胀率达到4.2%，此后一直徘徊在3.4%以上。
美国人的通货膨胀率保持在可控的 2% 水平已经近六年了。随着时间的推移，价格上涨，可能会挤压预算，这就是为什么在关键选举期间，价格对选民来说如此敏感。
在《卫报》最近与哈里斯民意调查一起进行的民意调查中，汽油价格是美国人最常见的痛点，83% 的人表示他们目前的财务状况正在受到影响。
显示美国平均汽油价格的折线图
伊朗战争开始后不久，世界五分之一的石油通常经过的重要航线霍尔木兹海峡就被封锁。它的关闭推高了世界各地的价格。尽管美国本身是主要石油生产国，但战后油价仍在飙升。根据 AAA 的数据，10 月中旬天然气平均价格为每加仑 4.32 美元，比一年前每加仑高出近 1.30 美元。
即使对于德克萨斯州这样的产油州，每加仑天然气的价格也为 3.81 美元，而一年前为 2.64 美元。与此同时，大部分天然气从海外进口的加利福尼亚州的司机支付每加仑 6.21 美元的费用。
劳动力市场是衡量经济健康状况的另一个指标，尽管自特朗普再次上任以来美国就业市场出现了一些增长，但去年的数据却出现了波动。 2025 年，经济总共新增 18.1 万个就业岗位，而 2024 年为 220 万个。

body_en: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash | Alaska
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash
Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Mary Peltola , a Democrat who is running for US Senate in Alaska , and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.

The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, said in a statement . “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”

Bruce added: “Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families.”

Police responded to a “multi-vehicle collision” at about 6.55pm on Saturday, according to the Anchorage police department. Peltola’s family and the occupant of a second vehicle were taken to a local hospital “with non-life-threatening injuries”, according to the authorities, while the occupant of a third vehicle refused medical transport.
“The circumstances of the collision are under investigation,” reads a statement from the police department.

Peltola, an Alaska Native and former congresswoman, is challenging Republican incumbent senator Dan Sullivan , hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the high-stakes race that has become one of the most watched in the nation.

On Friday, Donald Trump ordered the justice department to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Sullivan loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another Republican candidate who is listed on the ranked-choice ballot as Daniel J Sullivan Jr , who is a retired schoolteacher.

Peltola’s incident delayed what her campaign announced as the “Alaska Always tour,” an eight-stop push through the last week before election day. Her campaign said she will resume events on Tuesday, with a stop in Homer, Alaska.

阿拉斯加州参议员候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉因车祸推迟竞选活动
一名司机撞上前往竞选站的汽车运输队后，佩尔托拉和她的家人受轻伤
正在竞选阿拉斯加美国参议员的民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉 (Mary Peltola) 的竞选团队表示，她和家人周六在开车前往竞选站点时遭遇车祸，受了轻伤。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队在周日的一份声明中表示，当时一家人正在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会年度宴会的途中，另一辆车撞上了载着佩尔托拉及其家人的车辆。碰撞后佩尔托拉需要医疗救助。
佩尔托拉的竞选经理谢丽尔·布鲁斯在一份声明中说：“玛丽和她的家人受了轻伤，但精神状态良好。” “不幸的是，根据医疗专业人士的建议，玛丽即将在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将被重新安排在本周晚些时候，因为她需要时间来康复。”
布鲁斯补充道：“玛丽对这次事故推迟了她的阿拉斯加永远之旅的开始感到失望，她渴望回到竞选活动中，直接与阿拉斯加人谈论她的计划，即应对被操纵的系统并降低工薪家庭的成本。”
据安克雷奇警察局称，周六下午 6 点 55 分左右，警方对一起“多车相撞”事件做出了反应。当局称，佩尔托拉的家人和第二辆车的乘客被送往当地一家医院，“伤势没有生命危险”，而第三辆车的乘客拒绝接受医疗运送。
警察局的一份声明称：“碰撞情况正在调查中。”
阿拉斯加州原住民、前国会女议员佩尔托拉正在挑战共和党现任参议员丹·沙利文，希望成为近二十年来第一位在参议院代表该州的民主党人。两位候选人都试图争取阿拉斯加原住民选民的支持，阿拉斯加原住民选民是这场高风险竞选的关键选区，已成为全国最受关注的选区之一。
周五，唐纳德·特朗普命令司法部如果沙利文失败，将阻止阿拉斯加州参议院选举的认证。该诉讼指出，与另一位共和党候选人可能存在混淆，该候选人被列为排名选择选票的小丹尼尔·J·沙利文(Daniel J Sullivan Jr)，他是一名退休教师。
佩尔托拉的事件推迟了她的竞选团队宣布的“阿拉斯加永远巡回演出”，该巡回演出在选举日之前的最后一周进行八站巡演。她的竞选团队表示，她将于周二恢复活动，并在阿拉斯加荷马停留。

body_en: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan

President Donald Trump departs after speaking during a campaign rally at McMorran Place Sports and Entertainment Center, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Port Huron, Mich. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption

PORT HURON, Mich. — President Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally.
Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them

Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also repeatedly invoked the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93.

El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country "shameful" and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups. The Republican president's remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024.
"The president's statements are out of line," he said in a phone interview. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."

With Republicans on the defensive over inflation, soaring fuel prices and the Iran war, the president has been trying to generate turnout by claiming that El-Sayed and other Democrats are existential threats to America, instead of electoral rivals. Michigan's Senate race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is among a handful of contests that could determine control of the chamber.

Trump made his remarks in Port Huron, a Canadian border city about an hour north of Detroit and near communities where he made significant gains among Arab American voters in 2024. He became the first Republican presidential candidate since 2000 to win Dearborn, a city with one of the nation's largest concentrations of Arab Americans.

Trump, who imposed a travel ban targeting several predominantly Muslim countries during his first term, has increasingly leaned into anti-Muslim rhetoric as Election Day approaches. He also attacked Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota at Sunday's rally, where he declared that he had come to Michigan "to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator."
Responding to Trump, who also regularly mocks his name, El-Sayed told supporters at a rally in Grand Rapids later Sunday that he doesn't care how Trump pronounces or misrepresents it.
"I don't even care that he remembers my whole name because he can just go on and call me 'senator' after November," El-Sayed said, drawing cheers. "I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro."
El-Sayed's faith, associations and past statements become campaign flashpoints

Central to Republicans' strategy against El-Sayed in the final weeks of the campaign has been an effort to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamic movement with branches that the U.S. government has designated as terrorist organizations.

There is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. His half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, wrote on social media in 2012 that "my family has long been MB" and described a conversation with her mother about her involvement in the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1970s.
El-Sayed was born in the United States to Egyptian immigrant parents who divorced when he was young. He was raised by his father, not his biological mother.
Polls are a snapshot, and other helpful things to remember during the midterm elections
Trump on Sunday also targeted El-Sayed's ties to popular streamer Hasan Piker, who appeared alongside the Democrat multiple times during the primary campaign, including at his election night event.
Piker in the past has said that "Hamas is a thousand times better" than Israel, describing some Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and that "America deserved 9/11."

El-Sayed has faced criticism for his own rhetoric. He has repeatedly refused to answer questions about whether Iran or Israel poses a bigger threat to the country. Earlier this year, he said "hurt people hurt people" after an attack on a synagogue in the Detroit area. The attacker had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon the week earlier. El-Sayed later apologized, saying he was not trying to justify what happened.
body_zh: 特朗普在密歇根州升级了针对埃尔赛义德的反穆斯林攻击
2026 年 10 月 25 日星期日，唐纳德·特朗普总统在密歇根州休伦港麦克莫兰广场体育和娱乐中心举行的竞选集会上发表讲话后离开。朱莉娅·德马里·尼欣森/美联社隐藏标题栏
密歇根州休伦港——周日，唐纳德·特朗普总统强化了针对密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的反穆斯林言论，将他描绘成对国家安全的威胁，并质疑他对美国的忠诚度，其言论遭到了一位前阿拉伯裔美国盟友的严厉谴责。
共和党花费了数百万美元，但仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区
特朗普称前底特律卫生官员埃尔赛义德是“圣战分子”，“站在恐怖分子一边”，“在获准进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器”。他还多次援引2001年9月11日的恐怖袭击事件，将阻止埃尔赛义德进入参议院会议厅与联合航空93号航班上的劫机者进行反击的乘客进行比较。
如果当选，埃尔赛义德将成为该国第一位穆斯林参议员，他称针对他对国家忠诚的攻击是“可耻的”，并一再否认与极端主义团体有任何联系。这位共和党总统的言论遭到了特朗普阿拉伯裔美国人组织创始人比沙拉·巴巴(Bishara Bahbah)的谴责，该组织帮助领导总统在2024年向阿拉伯裔美国选民进行宣传。
“总统的言论不合时宜，”他在电话采访中说。 “他们正在跨越红线。他们是种族主义者。”
由于共和党在通货膨胀、燃油价格飙升和伊朗战争等问题上处于守势，总统一直试图通过声称埃尔赛义德和其他民主党人对美国的生存构成威胁，而不是选举竞争对手来提高投票率。埃尔-赛义德和共和党人迈克·罗杰斯之间的密歇根州参议院竞选是可能决定参议院控制权的少数竞争之一。
特朗普在加拿大边境城市休伦港发表讲话，该城市距离底特律以北约一小时车程，靠近社区，2024 年他在阿拉伯裔美国选民中获得了显着的支持。他成为 2000 年以来第一位赢得迪尔伯恩的共和党总统候选人，迪尔伯恩是美国阿拉伯裔美国人最集中的城市之一。
特朗普在第一个任期内对几个以穆斯林为主的国家实施了旅行禁令，随着选举日的临近，他越来越倾向于反穆斯林言论。他还在周日的集会上攻击了明尼苏达州的民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔，他在会上宣称自己来到密歇根州“是为了阻止圣战穆斯林兄弟会成员成为美国参议员”。
周日晚些时候，埃尔-赛义德在大急流城的一次集会上对支持者们说，他不在乎特朗普如何发音或歪曲它，以回应特朗普也经常嘲笑他的名字。
“我什至不在乎他是否记得我的全名，因为十一月之后他就可以继续叫我‘参议员’，”埃尔-赛义德说道，引来欢呼声。 “我将成为你的参议员穆罕默德，兄弟。”
埃尔-赛义德的信仰、关联和过去的言论成为竞选热点
共和党在竞选最后几周针对埃尔赛义德的战略核心是努力将他与穆斯林兄弟会联系起来，穆斯林兄弟会是一个伊斯兰运动，其分支已被美国政府指定为恐怖组织。
没有证据表明赛义德与穆斯林兄弟会有任何关系。他同父异母的妹妹伊曼·阿卜杜勒哈迪 (Eman Abdelhadi) 2012 年在社交媒体上写道，“我的家人长期以来一直是 MB”，并描述了与她母亲关于她在 20 世纪 70 年代初参与穆斯林兄弟会的对话。
埃尔-赛义德出生于美国，父母是埃及移民，他们在他年轻时就离婚了。他是由他的父亲抚养长大的，而不是他的亲生母亲。
民意调查只是一个快照，以及中期选举期间需要记住的其他有用的事情
特朗普周日还针对埃尔-赛义德与受欢迎的流媒体哈桑·皮克的关系，后者在初选期间多次与民主党一起出现，包括在他的选举之夜活动中。
皮克过去曾说过，“哈马斯比以色列强一千倍”，并将一些正统犹太人描述为“近亲繁殖”，并称“9/11是美国应得的”。
埃尔-赛义德因其言论而受到批评。他一再拒绝回答有关伊朗或以色列是否对该国构成更大威胁的问题。今年早些时候，他在底特律地区一座犹太教堂遭到袭击后表示，“受伤的人受伤了”。袭击者在一周前以色列对黎巴嫩的空袭中失去了四名亲属。埃尔-赛义德后来道歉，称他并不是想为所发生的事情辩护。

title_en: What are the US midterm elections and why do they matter?
title_zh: 什么是美国中期选举？它们为何如此重要？
summary: On 3 November, US citizens will decide whether Republicans will retain control of Congress or whether Democrats will come to power to stymie Trump’s agenda Donald Trump will still be US president on the morning of 4 November. But he could be facing a very diff
summary_zh: 11 月 3 日，美国公民将决定共和党是否会保留对国会的控制权，或者民主党是否会上台阻碍特朗普的执政。
body_en: On 3 November, US citizens will decide whether Republicans will retain control of Congress or whether Democrats will come to power to stymie Trump’s agenda

Donald Trump will still be US president on the morning of 4 November. But he could be facing a very different political landscape, depending on the results of the US midterm elections held the previous day.

As the name implies, midterm elections fall nearly halfway through a president’s term. They are often a telling referendum on the sitting president’s performance, something Trump is actively encouraging by telling voters “pretend I’m on the ballot”. In this case, voters will decide whether Trump’s Republican party can retain its grip on Congress.
All 435 seats in the House of Representatives. Republicans are defending a narrow majority, with Democrats needing a net gain of four seats to take control.

35 seats in the Senate. Thirty-three seats are up in regular elections, along with two special elections in Florida and Ohio to fill the remainder of terms that were vacated early. Republicans currently hold 53 seats, against 47 held by Democrats and independents who caucus with them. Democrats need to gain four seats to secure a majority.
39 governorships. Voters will choose governors in 36 states and three US territories.
Thousands of state legislative seats , as well as local offices, judicial contests and ballot measures on issues including taxes, abortion rights and voting rules.
body_zh: 11 月 3 日，美国公民将决定共和党是否会保留对国会的控制权，或者民主党是否会上台阻碍特朗普的议程
11 月 4 日上午，唐纳德·特朗普仍将担任美国总统。但他可能面临截然不同的政治格局，具体取决于前一天举行的美国中期选举的结果。
顾名思义，中期选举几乎在总统任期的一半时间进行。它们通常是对现任总统表现的一次有说服力的公投，特朗普通过告诉选民“假装我在选票上”来积极鼓励这一点。在这种情况下，选民将决定特朗普领导的共和党能否保住国会的控制权。
众议院全部435个席位。共和党正在捍卫微弱多数，而民主党需要净增加四个席位才能取得控制权。
参议院35个席位。常规选举中增加了 33 个席位，佛罗里达州和俄亥俄州还举行了两次特别选举，以填补提前空出的剩余任期。共和党目前拥有 53 个席位，而民主党和与他们同组的独立人士则拥有 47 个席位。民主党需要获得四个席位才能获得多数席位。
39个省长。选民将选出 36 个州和 3 个美国领地的州长。
数以千计的州立法席位以及地方办事处，就税收、堕胎权和投票规则等问题进行司法竞赛和投票措施。

title_en: Spurned by Trump, these outgoing Republicans aren’t helping their potential successors
title_zh: 被特朗普抛弃的这些即将离任的共和党人并没有帮助他们的潜在继任者
summary: They were snubbed on their way out of office. Their revenge is indifference.
summary_zh: 他们在卸任时遭到冷落。他们的报复是冷漠。
body_en: Republicans spurned by President Donald Trump aren't interested in rescuing their would-be replacements.
Instead, a growing number of retiring or ousted GOP incumbents from Nevada to North Carolina are sitting those races out, and in some cases, openly bucking their own party.

Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn has raised money for various Republican Senate candidates — just not for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who ousted him in the primary with support from Trump. He’s been vocal for months about what he sees as Paxton’s vulnerabilities and how Democrats could flip Texas blue for the first time in decades.

North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis — who has frequently criticized some of Trump’s Cabinet and broken with the White House on policy — has played little role in the campaign of former RNC Chair Michael Whatley, Trump’s hand-picked Senate candidate. The distance between the two Republicans is particularly notable as Whatley struggles to close the gap against Democrat Roy Cooper.
Rep. Mark Amodei has repeatedly criticized, and now openly rejected voting for , the GOP nominee to replace him, David Flippo.

“The bedwetting from outgoing moderate Republicans will define their legacy and only help socialists get elected,” said David McIntosh, president of the Trump-aligned Club for Growth, which has endorsed Flippo and Paxton. “People like John Cornyn and Mark Amodei need to get on board and support Republican nominees and stop posturing for an MSNOW contract.”

But other Republicans defended their colleagues: “I never would question the loyalty to the party of Thom Tillis or John Cornyn. Both of them have contributed immensely to our party and our party's successes in the past and I suspect will be going forward,” said North Dakota GOP Sen. Kevin Cramer. “But I also don't begrudge them for their opinions and their right to be open about them.”

These outgoing Republicans, several of whom were explicitly pushed out by Trump or persuaded to retire given his hold on the GOP, are using the midterms as a test: whether the party will demand loyalty to the president or can return to a pre-Trump era.

“What [Trump’s] done is created a coalition that, in my opinion, will not stay with Republicans once we go back to traditional Republican platform priorities,” Tillis said in a recent interview with POLITICO . “A lot of the elements of the populism that Trump created to expand a base that made him successful running for president, I don't think that stays with the party long-term.”

Some of those intraparty frustrations are starting to boil over, with Trump loyalist candidates and outgoing Republicans swiping at one another as Election Day barrels closer and the party’s overall fortunes look dire. The blame game is especially prominent in some of the Senate battlegrounds where Republicans have begun to quietly retreat in the final stretch of the midterms.

Tillis never followed through on his offers to help Whatley by reaching out to holdout donors in the North Carolina Senate race, said one person familiar with the campaign who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about internal matters.

"He was never part of our strategy because ... I mean, if he could have been helpful to us, then he could have ran," the person said, referring to Tillis' decision not to seek reelection last year. "The Tillis of the past year ain’t the same guy who worked overtime to help elect Republican majorities here in NC back in 2010."

One person with knowledge of Tillis and North Carolina politics, also granted anonymity to speak candidly, countered that the outgoing GOP senator “doesn’t help sure winners or sure losers" and "Whatley has been a sure loser throughout 2026, running as Donald Trump’s ‘guy,’ and making zero effort to build his own brand."

"All Whatley had to do was to keep this race competitive, but instead the party is facing a potential wipeout. This is an embarrassing effort by a former RNC chairman who only has himself and his consultants to blame for the completely avoidable beat down coming on Nov. 3," the person added.
Spokespeople for Tillis did not respond to a request for comment. Whatley's campaign declined to comment.

Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, touted the president’s endorsement record in a statement. More pointedly, she said that “Republicans who chose not to help elect other Republicans may as well be helping Democrats.”
The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
While the dynamic is less pronounced on the House side — Reps. Don Bacon and Elise Stefanik have been helpful to the Republicans running to replace them — there’s a clear exception: Amodei.

Flippo, who’s trying to replace him, has dealt with a host of scandals, from stolen valor accusations to carpetbagging to campaign finance issues , but Trump’s endorsement helped boost him through the Republican primary in June . Top Republican outside groups, including Club for Growth, have poured millions into his race in Nevada’s 2nd District to rescue a seat the president won by 14 points in 2024.
Amodei said in an interview that whoever was advising Trump to jump in and endorse Flippo gave “awful advice.”
body_zh: 被唐纳德·特朗普总统抛弃的共和党人对拯救他们的潜在继任者不感兴趣。
相反，从内华达州到北卡罗来纳州，越来越多退休或被赶下台的共和党现任议员拒绝参加这些竞选，在某些情况下，还公开反对自己的政党。
即将离任的参议员约翰·科宁 (John Cornyn) 为多位共和党参议院候选人筹集了资金，但没有为德克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿 (Ken Paxton) 筹集资金，后者在特朗普的支持下在初选中将他赶下台。几个月来，他一直直言不讳地谈论帕克斯顿的弱点，以及民主党如何能够在几十年来首次将德克萨斯州变成蓝色。
北卡罗来纳州参议员汤姆·蒂利斯（Thom Tillis）经常批评特朗普的一些内阁成员，并在政策上与白宫决裂。他在特朗普精心挑选的参议院候选人、共和党全国委员会前主席迈克尔·沃特利（Michael Whatley）的竞选活动中几乎没有发挥任何作用。由于沃特利正在努力缩小与民主党人罗伊·库珀的差距，两位共和党人之间的差距尤其引人注目。
众议员马克·阿莫迪 (Mark Amodei) 曾多次批评并公开拒绝投票给取代他的共和党提名人大卫·弗利波 (David Flippo)。
“即将离任的温和派共和党人的尿床将决定他们的政治遗产，并且只会帮助社会主义者当选，”与特朗普结盟的增长俱乐部主席戴维·麦金托什(David McIntosh)表示，该俱乐部支持弗利波和帕克斯顿。 “像 John Cornyn 和 Mark Amodei 这样的人需要加入并支持共和党提名人，并停止摆出争取 MSNOW 合同的姿态。”
但其他共和党人为他们的同事辩护：“我永远不会质疑汤姆·蒂利斯或约翰·科宁对政党的忠诚度。他们两人都为我们的政党以及我们政党过去的成功做出了巨大贡献，我怀疑他们将来也会继续前进，”北达科他州共和党参议员凯文·克莱默说。 “但我也不嫉妒他们的观点以及他们公开表达观点的权利。”
这些即将离任的共和党人，其中一些人被特朗普明确排挤，或者由于特朗普对共和党的控制而被说服退休，他们正在利用中期选举作为考验：共和党是否会要求效忠总统，或者能否回到特朗普之前的时代。
蒂利斯最近在接受《政治》杂志采访时表示：“我认为，一旦我们回到传统的共和党政纲优先事项，特朗普所做的就是创建一个联盟，这个联盟不会与共和党保持一致。” “特朗普为扩大选民基础而创造的许多民粹主义元素，使他成功竞选总统，但我认为这些元素不会长期存在于该党之中。”
随着选举日的临近，党内的一些不满情绪开始沸腾，特朗普的忠实候选人和即将卸任的共和党人互相攻击，而该党的整体命运看起来很糟糕。指责游戏在参议院的一些战场上尤其突出，共和党人在中期选举的最后阶段开始悄悄撤退。
一位熟悉竞选活动的人士表示，蒂利斯从未兑现他向北卡罗来纳州参议员竞选中坚持不懈的捐助者来帮助沃特利的提议，该人士被要求匿名坦率地谈论内部事务。
“他从来都不是我们战略的一部分，因为……我的意思是，如果他能够对我们有帮助，那么他就可以参选，”该人士说，他指的是蒂利斯去年决定不寻求连任。 “去年的蒂利斯与 2010 年加班加点帮助共和党在北卡罗来纳州选举多数席位的人已经不一样了。”
一位了解蒂利斯和北卡罗来纳州政治的人士也不愿透露姓名，他坦率地反驳说，即将离任的共和党参议员“无助于确定的赢家或输家”，并且“沃特利在整个 2026 年都是肯定的输家，作为唐纳德·特朗普的‘人’竞选，并为打造自己的品牌做出了零努力。”
“沃特利所要做的就是保持这场竞选的竞争力，但该党却面临着潜在的全军覆没。这是一位前共和党全国委员会主席的令人尴尬的举动，他只能将 11 月 3 日完全可以避免的失败归咎于他自己和他的顾问，”该人士补充道。
蒂利斯的发言人没有回应置评请求。沃特利的竞选团队拒绝发表评论。
共和党全国委员会发言人娜塔莉·巴尔达萨尔在一份声明中赞扬了总统的支持记录。更尖锐的是，她说“选择不帮助选举其他共和党人的共和党人也可能在帮助民主党人。”
白宫没有回应置评请求。
虽然众议院方面的动态不太明显——众议员唐·培根和埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克一直在帮助共和党竞选取代他们——但有一个明显的例外：阿莫代。
试图取代他的弗利波曾处理过一系列丑闻，从盗窃勇气指控到走私行为，再到竞选财务问题，但特朗普的支持帮助他在六月份的共和党初选中脱颖而出。包括增长俱乐部在内的顶级共和党外部团体已投入数百万美元参加他在内华达州第二选区的竞选，以挽救总统在 2024 年以 14 个百分点赢得的席位。
阿莫代在接受采访时表示，无论是谁建议特朗普加入并支持 Flippo，都给出了“糟糕的建议”。

title_en: Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race
title_zh: 布兰奇表示，特朗普并不是试图通过起诉参议院竞选来干预阿拉斯加州的选举结果
summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses the race
summary_zh: 司法部长托德·布兰奇正在为特朗普政府的诉讼辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止阿拉斯加州参议院结果的认证，如果现任共和党人
body_en: Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race - ABC News
Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race
Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses the race

WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Trump administration's lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses the race and argued that the legal challenge was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race .

President Donald Trump , who said Friday that he was "the one that said do it,” is not trying to overturn state election results “in any way, shape or form” on the cusp of the Nov. 3 election, Blanche told CNN's “State of the Union.”
“We wish that we didn’t have to do this. We hope for a resolution that works,” Blanche said.

Republicans fear that a second candidate on the ballot who is named Dan Sullivan — a retired teacher and school administrator from the tiny fishing community of Petersburg — could siphon away votes from the senator and tip the outcome in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola , a former congresswoman.

A day after the lawsuit was filed on Thursday, Peltola called it “just flagrant, flagrant corruption in my opinion” and a diversion tactic by Republicans. Alaska’s other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski, also criticized the lawsuit in a social media post.
Trump told reporters on Sunday that he believed the ballot was illegal because it was unfair and that Sen. Sullivan should be identified to voters as the sitting senator.
“At least let him use the name Sen. Dan Sullivan as opposed to incumbent, because a lot of people don’t know what incumbent means,” Trump said.
Alaskan voters will see “Dan S. Sullivan” identified as a “registered Republican” and “incumbent” on their ballots, while “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.” will not have a party affiliation.

Blanche represented Trump as a personal attorney before the Republican president appointed him to lead the Department of Justice, which filed the lawsuit in Alaska. Blanche defended Trump in his election inference case before voters elected Trump to a second White House term, effectively ending the criminal prosecution.
Amy Acton says Trump, Vance should 'look at the facts' after Ramaswamy attack ad
12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida university, police say
Airman killed rappelling from Alamodome's ceiling in Salute to Armed Forces ceremony

Blanche told CNN host Dana Bash that it was “crazy” for her to ask him if Trump was trying to lay the groundwork for the same sort of election challenges that occurred before a mob of his supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.

“We are not doing anything improper. We’re not doing anything we’re not allowed to do. And we have to let the process play out," Blanche said. "But I do think it’s important for the American people to understand that we are not — (and) President Trump is not — trying to take over a state election in any way shape or form.”
The lawsuit, he told CBS' “Face the Nation,” is meant to “put guardrails in place” to preserve possible evidence of voter confusion at the polls.

“It’s not saying, ‘Don’t certify.’ It’s saying, ‘If a court ultimately determines that it was decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters, then we do not think the states should certify.’ And that’s consistent with federal law and consistent with even Alaskan law, if that happens,” he said.
Associated Press writer Josh Boak contributed to this report.

布兰奇表示特朗普并不想通过起诉参议院竞选来干预阿拉斯加州的选举结果 - ABC News
司法部长托德·布兰奇正在为特朗普政府的诉讼辩护，如果现任共和党人丹·沙利文输掉竞选，该诉讼将阻止阿拉斯加州参议院结果的认证
华盛顿 - 华盛顿（美联社） - 周日，司法部长托德·布兰奇为特朗普政府提起的诉讼进行了辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止共和党现任议员丹·沙利文输掉阿拉斯加州参议院选举结果，并认为法律挑战是避免在备受关注的中期选举中让选民感到困惑的必要步骤。
布兰奇对 ​​CNN 的《国情咨文》节目表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统周五表示，他是“那个说要做就做的人”，他并没有试图在 11 月 3 日大选的风口浪尖上“以任何方式、形式”推翻州选举结果。
“我们希望我们不必这样做。我们希望能有一个有效的解决方案，”布兰奇说。
共和党人担心，选票上的第二位候选人丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）是一位来自彼得堡小渔村的退休教师和学校管理人员，他可能会从参议员那里夺走选票，并使选举结果有利于民主党人、前国会女议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）。
周四提起诉讼的第二天，佩尔托拉称其“在我看来是公然、公然的腐败”，也是共和党人的转移注意力的策略。阿拉斯加的另一位共和党参议员丽莎·默科斯基也在社交媒体帖子中批评了这起诉讼。
特朗普周日告诉记者，他认为这次投票是非法的，因为它不公平，并且应该向选民表明参议员沙利文是现任参议员。
“至少让他使用参议员丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）的名字，而不是现任参议员的名字，因为很多人不知道现任参议员的含义，”特朗普说。
阿拉斯加选民将在选票上看到“丹·S·沙利文”被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”，而“小丹尼尔·J·沙利文”则被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”。不会有党派关系。
在共和党总统任命布兰奇领导司法部之前，布兰奇作为特朗普的私人律师代表特朗普，司法部在阿拉斯加提起了诉讼。在选民选举特朗普连任白宫之前，布兰奇在选举推论案中为特朗普辩护，有效结束了刑事起诉。
艾米·阿克顿表示特朗普和万斯在拉马斯瓦米攻击广告后应该“看看事实”
警方称，佛罗里达大学附近发生枪击事件，造成 12 人受伤，其中包括 6 名儿童
飞行员在向武装部队致敬仪式上从阿拉莫圆顶天花板垂降时身亡
布兰奇告诉 CNN 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash)，她问他特朗普是否试图为 2021 年 1 月 6 日他的支持者暴徒冲进美国国会大厦之前发生的同样类型的选举挑战奠定基础，这太“疯狂”了。
“我们没有做任何不当的事情。我们没有做任何不被允许做的事情。我们必须让这个过程顺利进行，”布兰奇说。 “但我确实认为，美国人民必须明白，我们不会——（而且）特朗普总统也不会——试图以任何方式接管州选举。”
他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对全国”节目，该诉讼旨在“设置护栏”，以保留选民在投票时感到困惑的可能证据。
“这并不是说，‘不要认证’。而是说，‘如果法院最终认定该决定是由于混乱而不是选民的意愿而做出的，那么我们认为各州不应该认证。’这符合联邦法律，如果发生这种情况，甚至也符合阿拉斯加的法律，”他说。
美联社撰稿人乔什·博克对此报道做出了贡献。

Iranian officials said Sunday that indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue but that Tehran will not change its positions even if Mr. Trump does order a resumption of American attacks on the Islamic Republic.

Defense Minister Israel Katz on Monday rejected reports of a rift between Israel's army and its civilian leaders - most notably Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu - over the prospect of new strikes in the war with Iran as "entirely baseless."
Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive.

title_en: Peta releases video showing experiments on infant monkeys at University of Washington
title_zh: 善待动物组织发布视频，展示华盛顿大学对幼猴进行的实验
summary: Animal-rights group released video footage that shows distressed baby macaques undergoing lab experiments Footage released by the animal-rights group Peta reveals, for the first time, filmed experiments at the University of Washington’s National Primate Resear
summary_zh: 动物权利组织发布了视频片段，显示陷入困境的猕猴宝宝正在进行实验室实验动物权利组织发布的视频片段
body_en: Peta releases video showing experiments on infant monkeys at University of Washington
Animal-rights group released video footage that shows distressed baby macaques undergoing lab experiments

Footage released by the animal-rights group Peta reveals, for the first time, filmed experiments at the University of Washington’s National Primate Research Center (WaNPRC), in which newborn monkeys were separated from their mothers and subjected to neurological tests after prenatal exposure to a neurotoxin.

Records show that the infant monkeys, some just two days old, were used in research on domoic acid, a toxin produced by marine algae that accumulates in shellfish and can cause illness in humans. The experiments were part of a project that ran for six years until 2020.

The footage shows monkeys with electrodes attached to their heads, undergoing tests to investigate whether exposure to domoic acid in the womb had damaged their brains. The baby monkeys appear distressed as they clutch blankets, suck their fingers, screech, and jerk as experimenters shave their heads and test their reflexes and memory.

The infant macaques were bred at the University of Washington’s Infant Primate Research Laboratory for the project researching the developmental neurotoxicity of domoic acid in nonhuman primates . Researchers administered doses of domoic acid daily to 32 pregnant macaques . After birth, 28 infants were removed from their mothers, bottle-fed and kept in incubators before being housed individually at three weeks old.

“These monkeys are so young they still have the distinctive black fur of newborn macaques, yet instead of clinging to their mothers, they grasp blankets on metal tables , ” says Peta’s chief science adviser on primate issues, Dr Lisa Jones-Engel.

In the wild, macaques live in close social groups. Infants have long-term maternal care needs for their social and behavioral development, says Dr Malene Hansen, a long-tailed macaque expert, and cannot thrive without their mothers. “It is unethical to conduct research that separates infant macaques from their mothers. Period,” she says.

The WaNBRC told the Guardian: “We recognize that research involving infant animals raises important questions about their wellbeing. Maternal relationships and early social development are important considerations in nonhuman primate welfare. Our experienced veterinary and animal care personnel have specialized expertise in primate care, including nursery rearing.”

The project ran from 2014 to 2020 and received more than $4.2m in National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding. Some experiments lasted years. According to Peta, the monkeys were killed after the experiments were concluded.

The NIH says it takes the care and use of laboratory animals very seriously: “All animals used in NIH-supported research are protected by laws, regulations and policies designed to ensure the smallest possible number of animals are used and their welfare is prioritized.”
According to the WaNBRC, there are no current infant studies at its center; however, protocols for such studies are active.

Jones-Engel says: “There is no moral escape hatch. You can’t claim primates are used because they’re so like us, then take an infant away from its mother and experiment on it. You would never do that to a human primate. The cruelty also has biological consequences: maternal separation alters an infant’s physiology, immunity, behavior and development, distorting its response to the very substance or disease being studied.”

Jones-Engel worked as a primate scientist at the University of Washington for 17 years and has spent 35 years working as a primatologist. Her transition from animal researcher to campaigner is documented in a new film, Sentient .

Now one of the University of Washington’s most outspoken critics, Jones-Engel says the footage offers a rare glimpse into experiments involving monkeys: “For decades, the term ‘primate research’ has obscured the reality inside laboratories. These videos expose the suffering and raise a fundamental question: why are these facilities still operating at all?”
Peta is calling for the closure of all seven US National Primate Research Centers .

The footage relates to a research program that has operated at the University of Washington’s Infant Primate Research Laboratory since 1971 and emerges amid a long-running dispute between Peta and the university. In a 2020 lawsuit, Peta challenged the school’s handling of public-records requests. The court ruled that the university violated laws by failing to adequately search for records, in a case that revealed systematic destruction of photos and videos at the school.
‘They know they’re safe’: beagles saved from US research facility after protests
The footage was released to Peta in September 2026 in response to a records request. The videos were filmed between 2017 and 2019.
The WaNPRC says the monkey studies have contributed to an understanding how prenatal domoic acid exposure may affect learning and memory: “These findings remain relevant to public health.”
body_zh: 善待动物组织发布视频，展示华盛顿大学对幼猴进行的实验
动物权利组织发布了视频片段，显示痛苦的小猕猴正在进行实验室实验
动物权利组织 Peta 发布的视频首次揭示了在华盛顿大学国家灵长类动物研究中心 (WaNPRC) 拍摄的实验，其中新生猴子在产前接触神经毒素后被与母亲分开，并接受神经系统测试。
记录显示，这些小猴子（有些刚出生两天）被用于研究软骨藻酸，软骨藻酸是一种由海藻产生的毒素，积聚在贝类中，可导致人类患病。这些实验是一个持续六年直至 2020 年的项目的一部分。
这段视频显示，猴子的头上装有电极，正在接受测试，以调查在子宫内暴露于软骨藻酸是否损害了它们的大脑。当实验人员剃光头并测试他们的反应和记忆力时，小猴子们抓着毯子、吸吮手指、尖叫和抽搐，显得很痛苦。
这些猕猴幼崽是在华盛顿大学婴儿灵长类动物研究实验室培育的，用于研究软骨藻酸对非人类灵长类动物的发育神经毒性。研究人员每天给 32 只怀孕的猕猴服用一定剂量的软骨藻酸。 28 名婴儿出生后就被从母亲身边抱走，用奶瓶喂养并放在保温箱中，然后在三周大时被单独饲养。
善待动物组织灵长类问题首席科学顾问丽莎·琼斯-恩格尔博士表示：“这些猴子还太小，仍然保留着新生猕猴特有的黑色皮毛，但它们不会紧贴母亲，而是抓住金属桌子上的毯子。”
在野外，猕猴生活在紧密的社会群体中。长尾猕猴专家马琳·汉森博士表示，婴儿的社会和行为发展需要长期的母亲护理，没有母亲就无法茁壮成长。 “进行将猕猴幼崽与母亲分开的研究是不道德的。就这样，”她说。
WaNBRC 告诉《卫报》：“我们认识到，涉及幼年动物的研究提出了有关它们福祉的重要问题。母性关系和早期社会发展是非人类灵长类动物福利的重要考虑因素。我们经验丰富的兽医和动物护理人员在灵长类动物护理（包括保育）方面拥有专业知识。”
该项目从 2014 年持续到 2020 年，获得了美国国立卫生研究院 (NIH) 超过 420 万美元的资助。有些实验持续了数年。据善待动物组织称，实验结束后猴子就被杀死了。
NIH 表示，它非常重视实验动物的护理和使用：“NIH 支持的研究中使用的所有动物都受到法律、法规和政策的保护，旨在确保使用尽可能少的动物，并优先考虑它们的福利。”
根据 WaNBRC 的说法，其中心目前没有婴儿研究；然而，此类研究的方案仍然有效。
琼斯-恩格尔说：“不存在道德逃生舱口。你不能声称灵长类动物被利用，因为它们与我们如此相似，然后将婴儿从母亲身边带走并进行实验。你永远不会对人类灵长类动物这样做。这种残忍行为也会产生生物学后果：母亲的分离会改变婴儿的生理、免疫力、行为和发育，扭曲其对所研究的物质或疾病的反应。”
琼斯-恩格尔在华盛顿大学担任了 17 年的灵长类动物科学家，并作为一名灵长类动物学家工作了 35 年。她从动物研究员到活动家的转变记录在一部新电影《Sentient》中。
琼斯-恩格尔现在是华盛顿大学最直言不讳的批评者之一，他说这段视频让我们难得一睹涉及猴子的实验：“几十年来，‘灵长类研究’这个词掩盖了实验室内的现实。这些视频揭露了痛苦，并提出了一个基本问题：为什么这些设施仍然在运行？”
善待动物组织呼吁关闭所有七个美国国家灵长类动物研究中心。
这段视频与华盛顿大学婴儿灵长类研究实验室自 1971 年以来一直运行的一项研究项目有关，该项目是在善待动物组织与该大学之间长期存在的争议中出现的。在 2020 年的一场诉讼中，善待动物组织对学校处理公共记录请求的方式提出了质疑。法院裁定，该大学未能充分搜索记录，违反了法律，该案件揭露了学校系统性销毁照片和视频的行为。
“他们知道自己很安全”：抗议后美国研究机构救出了小猎犬
应记录要求，这段视频于 2026 年 9 月发布给善待动物组织。这些视频于 2017 年至 2019 年拍摄。
WaNPRC 表示，猴子研究有助于了解产前软骨藻酸暴露如何影响学习和记忆：“这些发现仍然与公共健康相关。”

title_en: Sunlight at night: US startup’s demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws critcism
title_zh: 夜间阳光：美国初创公司演示从太空照亮地球遭批评
summary: Company imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals Locals in a rural area of California were recently startled to see dazzlingly bright light shining down from nearby mountains at n
summary_zh: 该公司模仿镜子反射太阳光，引起了一些科学家、环保主义者和加州当地人的反对。
body_en: Sunlight at night: US startup’s demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws critcism
Company imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals
Locals in a rural area of California were recently startled to see dazzlingly bright light shining down from nearby mountains at night, illuminating a swathe of the desert below.
Unbeknown to them, the strange nocturnal illumination was the latest step in a company’s plan to erect thousands of giant mirrors in space to reflect sunlight on to the Earth during night-time.

The night-time light demonstration, near the town of Lone Pine in the Sierra Nevada region, was conducted by a US startup called Reflect Orbital , which has an almost sci-fi aim to launch 50,000 satellites into space in the next decade to illuminate parts of the world at night.

In July, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approved Reflect Orbital’s proposal to launch an initial demonstration satellite next year, which will orbit the Earth and, via a 59ft-diameter mirror, reflect sunlight in 3-mile-wide beams in strengths from moonlight up to the brightness of the sun at noon.

The demonstration in California, undertaken earlier this month, showcased what this would look like on the ground, to the bewilderment of locals, one of whom called the lights “blinding”. Large mobile lights were erected near Mount Whitney, with Reflect Orbital comparing the radiance to that of a full moon.

This provided, the company said, a realistic simulation of one of the benefits of this technology: to help search-and-rescue teams and other emergency responders at night. Other planned uses include bathing crops in sunlight, replacing broken streetlights and even providing solar power for military operations, all summoned by the tap of a button on an app.

“Search-and-rescue teams are expected to be our first customers, so this was a real-world test conducted alongside teams who would use our technology,” said a spokesperson for Reflect Orbital, which partnered with a local search-and-rescue team for the demonstration.
“We’ll keep working closely with local communities and authorities wherever we operate, and are excited to show how this technology can help save lives.”

A coalition of environmentalists and astronomers are far less excited about Reflect Orbital’s ambitions, however . These groups have criticized the company and the FCC for threatening a harmful change to the separation of night and day that will affect everything from people’s sleep to wildlife and the ability to see the stars from Earth.

“This is an idiotic project,” said Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney with Earthjustice, an environmental group. “There are a huge number of unresolved questions and significant potential impacts. Literally all of life on Earth evolved based on the rhythm of day and night and there is a ton of data showing that messing with this is not a good idea.”

“There needs to be some sort of discussion and analysis before we grant these people the right to fundamentally alter the night sky,” he added. “The proposal for 50,000 of these satellite mirrors is crazy and would really end the night sky as we know it.”
Bomb the Arctic, dam the Mediterranean and build a second moon: five outlandish plans to remodel our climate

In August, four groups represented by Earthjustice asked the FCC to reconsider its approval , citing concerns that opening up the skies to mirrored satellites, which would ascend to about 400 miles (645km) above the Earth’s surface before reflecting light back, would cause a litany of problems.
Animals such as birds, insects and mammals rely on the reliable change between day and night to feed, shelter and mate, with any change to this being potentially disastrous for some species.

Astronomers, meanwhile, have complained that this night-time glare would worsen existing light pollution and spur an overall rush to add more satellites to orbit – Elon Musk’s SpaceX plans to place 1 million celestial datacenters around Earth – that will obscure the stars and cause more space debris that could descend as pollution back to our world.

There are also concerns that the scrambling of night and day will harm people’s health by disrupting their circadian rhythms as they sleep. Looking directly at the unusual glaring sunlight at night would also, much like doing so during a solar eclipse, harm people’s eyes.

Reflect Orbital has said its technology will actually aid the environment by boosting the energy output of solar panels when sunlight is pointed at them during night-time, thereby reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

But some climate scientists have warned against meddling with the amount of sun’s energy reaching Earth. Proposals for solar geoengineering , in which particles are sprayed into the atmosphere to deflect sunlight away from Earth instead of toward it, have also prompted fierce opposition .
body_zh: 夜间阳光：美国初创公司演示从太空照亮地球遭批评
该公司模仿镜子反射太阳光，遭到一些科学家、环保主义者和加州当地人的反对
加利福尼亚州农村地区的当地人最近惊讶地发现，夜间附近的山脉发出耀眼的光芒，照亮了下面的大片沙漠。
他们不知道的是，这种奇怪的夜间照明是一家公司计划的最新一步，该计划旨在在太空中安装数千面巨型镜子，以在夜间将阳光反射到地球上。
内华达山脉地区孤松镇附近的夜间灯光演示是由一家名为 Reflect Orbital 的美国初创公司进行的，该公司的目标近乎科幻，即在未来十年内向太空发射 50,000 颗卫星，在夜间照亮世界部分地区。
今年 7 月，美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 批准了 Reflect Orbital 的提议，将于明年发射一颗初始演示卫星，该卫星将绕地球运行，并通过直径 59 英尺的镜子，以 3 英里宽的光束反射阳光，其强度从月光到中午太阳的亮度。
本月早些时候在加利福尼亚州进行的示威活动向当地人展示了这种景象，令当地人感到困惑，其中一人称这些灯光“令人眼花缭乱”。惠特尼山附近竖起了大型移动灯，反射轨道将其亮度与满月的亮度进行了比较。
该公司表示，这提供了对该技术的好处之一的真实模拟：在夜间帮助搜救队和其他应急响应人员。其他计划的用途包括让农作物沐浴在阳光下、更换破损的路灯，甚至为军事行动提供太阳能，所有这些都可以通过点击应用程序上的按钮来实现。
Reflect Orbital 的发言人表示：“预计搜救队将成为我们的第一批客户，因此这是与使用我们技术的团队一起进行的真实测试。”该公司与当地搜救队合作进行了演示。
“无论我们在哪里开展业务，我们都将继续与当地社区和当局密切合作，并很高兴展示这项技术如何帮助拯救生命。”
然而，环保主义者和天文学家联盟对 Reflect Orbital 的雄心壮志却远没有那么兴奋。这些团体批评该公司和联邦通信委员会威胁要对昼夜分离进行有害的改变，这将影响从人们的睡眠到野生动物以及从地球上看到星星的能力等一切。
“这是一个愚蠢的项目，”环保组织地球正义的高级律师扬·哈塞尔曼说。 “还有大量未解决的问题和重大的潜在影响。实际上，地球上的所有生命都是根据昼夜节律进化的，大量数据表明，扰乱这一点并不是一个好主意。”
“在我们授予这些人从根本上改变夜空的权利之前，需要进行某种讨论和分析，”他补充道。 “建造 50,000 个卫星镜的提议太疯狂了，这真的会终结我们所知的夜空。”
轰炸北极、在地中海筑坝并建造第二颗卫星：重塑气候的五个古怪计划
8月，以地球正义为代表的四个组织要求联邦通信委员会重新考虑其批准，理由是担心向镜像卫星开放天空会导致一系列问题，镜像卫星将上升到距地球表面约400英里（645公里）的高度，然后将光反射回来。
鸟类、昆虫和哺乳动物等动物依赖昼夜的可靠变化来进食、庇护和交配，这种变化对某些物种来说可能是灾难性的。
与此同时，天文学家抱怨说，这种夜间眩光会加剧现有的光污染，并促使人们热衷于将更多卫星送入轨道——埃隆·马斯克的 SpaceX 计划在地球周围放置 100 万个天体数据中心——这将遮蔽恒星，并产生更多的太空碎片，这些碎片可能作为污染落回我们的世界。
还有人担心，昼夜交替会扰乱睡眠时的昼夜节律，从而损害人们的健康。夜间直视不寻常的刺眼阳光也会伤害人们的眼睛，就像在日食期间这样做一样。
Reflect Orbital 表示，其技术实际上可以通过在夜间阳光照射时提高太阳能电池板的能量输出来帮助环境，从而减少对化石燃料的依赖。
但一些气候科学家警告不要干预到达地球的太阳能量。太阳能地球工程的提议也引发了激烈的反对，该提议将粒子喷射到大气中，使阳光远离地球而不是朝向地球。

title_en: Israeli military closing West Bank crossings before elections
title_zh: 以色列将在军事行动期间在选举前关闭西岸过境点
summary: The Israeli military's operation comes in response to a gun attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others in the West Bank.
summary_zh: 以色列军方采取行动是为了回应西岸发生的枪击事件，该事件造成两名以色列士兵死亡、三人受伤。
body_en: Israeli military closing West Bank crossings ahead of upcoming elections as massive operation continues - CBS News
The Israeli military continued a massive operation in the occupied West Bank, placing major restrictions on movement ahead of Israel's upcoming elections.

The operation, which comes in response to a shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others in Hebron on Friday, has displaced hundreds of Palestinians over the last two days.

In Hebron, more than 2,700 people have been displaced from their homes, including hundreds of children, Palestinian officials said Sunday. Since Friday's attack, all entrances and exits to the city have remained sealed, with the epicenter of the operation in Deir Bahha and another part of the city called Al-Jalda, according to Hebron Mayor Yousef Zuhair Al-Jabari.
"People cannot reach or enter the city, and they cannot leave it. The blockade has affected every aspect of life," Al-Jabari said.
The Israeli military said it operated in more than 400 different locations over the weekend and arrested 40 Palestinians it claimed were affiliated with Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad.

Additionally, the Israeli military said most Palestinian workers with permits will not be allowed to enter Israeli settlements for work on Sunday and Monday, and crossings into Israel will remain closed until after Tuesday's Israeli elections.
The election is largely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's leadership and security policies during the past three years of war.

Six Israelis have been killed this year in attacks in the West Bank, which is experiencing a surge of violence . During the same period, 112 Palestinians have been killed, according to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Health Ministry.

Friday's attack sparked outrage in Israel, with Netanyahu and three members of his right-wing government giving statements from the site of the attack on Friday afternoon, vowing to respond forcefully .
"We warned a few weeks ago about attempts by our enemies to harm us, our citizens and our soldiers ahead of the election," Netanyahu said. "We will act to destroy this place."

Netanyahu, who is running for reelection in next week's elections and has received President Trump's endorsement , is under pressure to demonstrate a strong show of force against Palestinian attackers to bolster his image for Israelis concerned with security.

Roughly 3 million Palestinians and 540,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Mideast war. Hebron is one of its most tense cities and the only place where Jewish settlers live in the heart of a densely populated Palestinian area under Israeli military protection.

以色列军方继续在被占领的约旦河西岸开展大规模行动，在以色列即将举行的选举之前对人员流动实施重大限制。
此次行动是为了回应周五在希伯伦发生的枪击事件，造成两名以色列士兵死亡、三人受伤，过去两天已导致数百名巴勒斯坦人流离失所。
巴勒斯坦官员周日表示，在希伯伦，已有 2,700 多人流离失所，其中包括数百名儿童。希伯伦市长尤瑟夫·祖海尔·贾巴里 (Yousef Zuhair Al-Jabari) 表示，自周五袭击事件以来，该市的所有出入口均保持封锁，行动的中心位于代尔巴哈 (Deir Bahha) 和该市另一个名为阿尔贾尔达 (Al-Jalda) 的地区。
“人们无法到达或进入这座城市，也无法离开它。封锁影响了生活的方方面面，”贾巴里说。
以色列军方表示，周末在 400 多个不同地点开展行动，逮捕了 40 名据称与哈马斯或巴勒斯坦伊斯兰圣战组织有关联的巴勒斯坦人。
此外，以色列军方表示，大多数持有许可证的巴勒斯坦工人将不被允许在周日和周一进入以色列定居点工作，进入以色列的过境点将保持关闭，直到周二以色列选举之后。
此次选举在很大程度上被视为对总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在过去三年战争期间的领导和安全政策的公投。
今年，六名以色列人在约旦河西岸的袭击中丧生，该地区的暴力事件正在激增。据位于拉马拉的巴勒斯坦卫生部称，同一时期有 112 名巴勒斯坦人被杀。
周五的袭击引发了以色列的愤怒，内塔尼亚胡和他的右翼政府的三名成员周五下午在袭击现场发表声明，誓言要采取强有力的回应。
内塔尼亚胡说：“几周前，我们警告我们的敌人企图在选举前伤害我们、我们的公民和我们的士兵。” “我们将采取行动摧毁这个地方。”
内塔尼亚胡正在下周的选举中竞选连任，并已获得特朗普总统的支持，他面临着向巴勒斯坦袭击者展示强力武力的压力，以提升他在关心安全的以色列人中的形象。
约 300 万巴勒斯坦人和 54 万以色列定居者居住在以色列在 1967 年中东战争中占领的约旦河西岸。希伯伦是局势最紧张的城市之一，也是以色列军事保护下人口稠密的巴勒斯坦地区中心唯一有犹太定居者居住的地方。

body_en: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj ’s behind.

Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.
“You are a great athlete,” Trump also said to Husted. “Congratulations.”

Trump was speaking at the rally to support Mike Rogers , the Michigan Republican Senate candidate. The Michigan race between Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed remains neck and neck as both political parties scramble for control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections . But he couldn’t resist his purported other favorite topic.

This afternoon, Trump said the media buzz about these comments was “fake news” neglecting the athletic context of his statements. Trump said he had just learned Husted was a college athlete when he was “looking at him up and down, and I’m studying him”.

Trump insisted his subsequent crack was “in fun”. “I said: I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record, women yes, men no, OK.”
Trump then shouted out Minaj, who the New York Post said was donned in “head-to-toe Gucci” today. Minaj, the paper also reported, was seen walking with Trump after leaving Air Force One.
“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before – Nicki Minaj ,” Trump said, prompting celebratory woos from the crowd. “That’s hard to miss. That – stand up! That’s hard to miss.
“OK, I’m going to get back to my story, Nicki,” Trump continued following still more cheers. “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time.”
Trump made statements about Husted’s tush just over a week ago in Kentucky.

“I examined his ass,” Trump said of Husted, who was not at the event. “And then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline. Studied him. He’s got a jawline.
“I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering,” Trump said.
Trump also recently praised the appearance of Ed Gallrein, theRepublican congressional candidate from Kentucky.
Obama rallies rapturous Michigan crowd for El-Sayed: ‘He’ll finish the job we started’

“I needed somebody good, and this guy walks through the door,” Trump remarked of Gallrein, in describing his efforts to find a replacement for anti-Maga incumbent Thomas Massie. “I said, look at this beautiful guy.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why Trump has been discussing others’ bodies.
Trump’s comments come amid criticism of his language style, which some have likened to grotesquerie.
body_zh: 特朗普在密歇根州为迈克·罗杰斯和妮琪·米娜的臀部集会
特朗普再次祝贺俄亥俄州参议员的臀部，然后厚颜无耻地评论说唱歌手“很难错过”
唐纳德·特朗普周日在密歇根州的一次集会上重申了他对丰满臀部的热爱，他鼓励人群称赞说唱歌手妮琪·米娜的臀部。
特朗普在解释他最近对俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德臀部的观察时，对米娜的臀部做出了厚颜无耻的评论。十月初，特朗普谈到这位前大学橄榄球运动员时说：“我不经常对男人这样做。我开始检查他的身体，因为我不知道他是一名伟大的运动员。我上下观察。我看着他的屁股，我看着整个 - 然后我看着他的手。看看他的手。他有这些，就像爪子。
“你是一位伟大的运动员，”特朗普还对赫斯特德说。 “恭喜。”
特朗普在支持密歇根州共和党参议员候选人迈克·罗杰斯的集会上发表讲话。罗杰斯和民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德在密歇根州的竞选仍然不相上下，因为两个政党都在即将到来的中期选举中争夺国会的控制权。但他无法抗拒他所谓的另一个最喜欢的话题。
今天下午，特朗普表示媒体对这些言论的热议是“假新闻”，忽视了他言论的运动背景。特朗普表示，当他“上下打量他，我正在研究他”时，他刚刚得知赫斯特德是一名大学运动员。
密歇根州居民反对潜在的 64 亿美元数据中心账单：“这太疯狂了”
特朗普坚称他随后的破解是“有趣的”。 “我说：我看着他的屁股，我以前从来没有对男人做过这样的事。这是真的。私下里，女人可以，男人不行，好吧。”
特朗普随后大声喊出米娜，《纽约邮报》称米娜今天“从头到脚都穿着古驰”。该报还报道称，有人看到米娜在离开空军一号后与特朗普一起散步。
“顺便说一句，我以前看过一个非常漂亮的屁股——妮琪·米娜，”特朗普说道，引发了人群的欢呼。 “这很难错过。那个——站起来！那很难错过。
“好吧，我要回到我的故事了，尼基，”特朗普在更多的欢呼声中继续说道。 “我希望尼基没有受到侮辱，但我们爱尼基。她和我们在一起很长时间了。”
特朗普一周前在肯塔基州就赫斯特德的言论发表了声明。
“我检查了他的屁股，”特朗普谈到没有出席活动的赫斯特德时说道。 “然后我看着他的肩膀。我看着他的脚。我看着他的手。我看着他的下巴轮廓。研究他。他有下巴轮廓。
“然后我拍了拍他的肩膀，它就像一块钢铁。我还在康复中，”特朗普说。
特朗普最近还赞扬了来自肯塔基州的共和党国会候选人埃德·加莱因(Ed Gallrein)的亮相。
奥巴马为埃尔赛义德召集密歇根州狂热的人群：“他将完成我们开始的工作”
“我需要一个好人，而这个人走进了大门，”特朗普在描述他为寻找反马加现任托马斯·马西替代者的努力时这样评价加莱因。 “我说，看看这个漂亮的家伙。”
白宫没有立即回应有关特朗普为何一直讨论他人尸体的置评请求。
特朗普发表此番言论之际，他的语言风格受到批评，有些人将其比喻为怪诞。

title_en: Redistricting isn't playing out how the GOP hoped. And, Brazil's Lula wins 4th term
title_zh: 选区重新划分并没有达到共和党所希望的效果。并且，巴西卢拉赢得第四个任期
summary: Republicans are spending millions on the midterms, and they still may not win districts drawn to favor them. And, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in a stunning political comeback.
summary_zh: 共和党在中期选举上花费了数百万美元，但他们仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区。还有巴西的路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦
body_en: Up First briefing: GOP redistricting; France, Serbia protests; Brazil election : NPR

Up First briefing: GOP redistricting; France, Serbia protests; Brazil election Republicans are spending millions on the midterms, and they still may not win districts drawn to favor them. And, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in a stunning political comeback.

Redistricting isn't playing out how the GOP hoped. And, Brazil's Lula wins 4th term
GOP Redistricting Bust, Lula Wins Brazil Election, Protest Spread In Europe

North Carolina Republican Congressional candidates, State Rep. Jennifer Balkcom and Laurie Buckhout (R) are embraced by President Trump during an election rally on October 20, 2026 in Greenville, North Carolina. Buckhout is running in North Carolina's 1st District which was redrawn to heavily favor Republicans and is now a toss-up. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images hide caption

Republicans had a plan to keep control of the House in the midterms: Redraw congressional district lines to favor the GOP and avoid the historical pattern of heavy midterm losses. President Trump began pressuring Republican-led states to do just that last year, but it isn't working out as expected. Republicans could now be spending millions of dollars on House seats that were supposed to be easy wins, and end up losing anyway . Of the 15 districts drawn specifically to favor Republicans, only five are rated by the Cook Political Report as either likely or solid Republican. Most are toss-ups or lean toward a Democratic win.

🎧 One reason the Republicans' redistricting push hasn't been as successful as expected is that some district lines were drawn based on the 2024 Trump electorate, NPR's Tamara Keith tells Up First . Since then, his support has weakened , particularly among young and Latino voters. Several Democratic incumbents targeted by redistricting have stuck it out to fight for their seats. A Republican strategist involved with midterm races, but who wasn't authorized to speak publicly, pushed back on the characterization that redistricting didn't work, saying that it "creates new battlefields" but doesn't "create outcomes."

➡️ The NPR App has all of NPR's election coverage in one place — from the biggest stories across the country, to the issues that matter close to home. Browse headlines, playlists, podcast episodes, videos and more, all on the 2026 Election tab .

In a stunning political comeback, leftist Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in the presidential runoff election in Brazil. Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro , son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, by more than 4 million votes. It's the first time since Brazil restored democracy in 1989 that a candidate who finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidency.

🎧 Lula's win appears to have put the brake on a right-wing sweep in Latin America, NPR's Carrie Kahn says. Seven conservative presidents have been elected in the past 18 months. Kahn says one message helped rally voters in the final weeks of Lula's campaign: that the return of a Bolsonaro to power would be an existential threat to Brazilian democracy.

Large demonstrations against the government continued over the weekend in France, where more than 100,000 people showed up in Paris, and more than 400,000 came out nationwide. What started with students demanding better conditions has grown into a much bigger movement. Unions and public-sector workers have joined, calling for more public spending and protesting growing inequality. Similar protests have erupted across Europe, from Spain to Serbia.

🎧 The reasons behind the protests vary, from schools and housing costs to corruption, NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says. But they have something in common: most are leaderless movements by young people frustrated with the world they're being left to. In Serbia, crowds celebrated in the streets of Belgrade after a student-led movement known as the "student-list" defeated the party of longtime strongman Aleksandar Vucic in Sunday's parliamentary elections. The win followed two years of protests over government corruption and lack of accountability.

Out-of-pocket maternity expenses are difficult to predict. A federal requirement for insurers to provide personalized cost estimates under the No Surprises Act was supposed to take effect in 2022, but federal regulators haven't made it happen despite pressure from Congress. Until the cost of maternity care gets more transparent, here are some tips to help you budget for the cost of pregnancy
👶 Enroll your baby in your insurance before your deadline. For most employer health plans, that's within 30 days of birth.
👶 Check what your maximum out-of-pocket expense is. That's the most you'll pay each year for covered, in-network expenses before your insurance pays 100% of the costs.
👶 Choose in-network providers whenever possible.
👶 Go over every bill, and don't be afraid to appeal errors.
👶 Ask your hospital or other providers about financial assistance.
