共和党重新划分选区失败，卢拉赢得巴西大选，欧洲抗议蔓延
北卡罗来纳州共和党国会候选人、州众议员詹妮弗·巴尔克科姆 (Jennifer Balkcom) 和劳里·巴克豪特 (Laurie Buckhout)（右）于 2026 年 10 月 20 日在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔举行的选举集会上受到特朗普总统的拥抱。巴克豪特在北卡罗来纳州第一选区竞选，该选区经过重新划定以大力支持共和党，现在是一个难以预测的局面。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏

共和党人有一个在中期选举中保持对众议院控制权的计划：重新划定国会选区界限以支持共和党，并避免中期选举惨败的历史模式。特朗普总统去年开始向共和党领导的各州施压，要求他们这样做，但效果并不如预期。共和党人现在可能会花费数百万美元来赢得本应轻松获胜的众议院席位，但无论如何最终都会失败。在专门为共和党选区的 15 个选区中，只有 5 个选区被库克政治报告评为可能或坚定的共和党人。大多数都是犹豫不决或倾向于民主党获胜。

🎧 NPR 的塔玛拉·基思 (Tamara Keith) 告诉 Up First，共和党的选区重划行动没有像预期那样成功的原因之一是，一些选区划分是根据 2024 年特朗普选民的情况绘制的。从那时起，他的支持率有所减弱，特别是在年轻和拉丁裔选民中。几位成为选区重新划分目标的民主党现任议员坚持不懈地争取席位。一位参与中期选举但未被授权公开发言的共和党战略家反驳了选区重新划分不起作用的说法，称这“创造了新的战场”，但并没有“创造结果”。

左翼人士路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦在巴西总统决选中赢得了第四个任期，取得了惊人的政治复兴。卢拉以超过 400 万票击败了前极右翼总统雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗的儿子弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗。这是自1989年巴西恢复民主以来，首次由在第一轮中获得第二名的候选人最终赢得总统宝座。
NPR 的卡丽·卡恩 (Carrie Kahn) 表示，卢拉的胜利似乎给右翼在拉丁美洲的横扫踩下了刹车。过去 18 个月内选出了 7 位保守派总统。卡恩表示，在卢拉竞选的最后几周，有一条信息帮助团结了选民：博尔索纳罗重新掌权将对巴西民主构成生存威胁。

Large demonstrations against the government continued over the weekend in France, where more than 100,000 people showed up in Paris, and more than 400,000 came out nationwide.最初的学生要求更好的条件已经发展成为一场更大的运动。工会和公共部门工人也加入进来，呼吁增加公共支出并抗议日益严重的不平等。从西班牙到塞尔维亚，欧洲各地都爆发了类似的抗议活动。

🎧 NPR 的埃莉诺·比尔兹利 (Eleanor Beardsley) 表示，抗议背后的原因各不相同，从学校和住房成本到腐败。但它们有一些共同点：大多数都是由对自己所处的世界感到沮丧的年轻人发起的无领导运动。在塞尔维亚，学生领导的名为“学生名单”的运动在周日的议会选举中击败了长期强人亚历山大·武契奇的政党后，人群在贝尔格莱德街头庆祝。这场胜利是在针对政府腐败和缺乏问责制的抗议活动进行了两年之后取得的。

title_en: Japan indicts U.S. Marine on murder charge over woman's killing
title_zh: 日本起诉美国海军陆战队员谋杀妇女
summary: Police arrested Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, on suspicion of strangling Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel.
summary_zh: 警方逮捕了兰斯下士。 20 岁的德文·雅各布·巴拉德 (Devin Jacob Ballard) 涉嫌在一家酒店勒死 39 岁的安娜·八木 (Anna Yagi)。
body_en: U.S. Marine indicted on murder charge over woman's killing in Japan - CBS News
Japanese prosecutors have indicted a U.S. Marine on suspicion of murdering a woman on Okinawa, a court spokesman told AFP on Monday, in a case that prompted public outrage.
The alleged killing of the 39-year-old Japanese woman caused Japan's premier to slam the "heinous crime" and reignited controversy over the heavy U.S. military presence on the southern island.
"The case was indicted on October 25," said the spokesman for the court in Naha, confirming media reports that the suspect had been indicted on charges of murder and robbery.

Okinawa prefectural police said they arrested Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard , 20, who is stationed at Futenma Air Station, on suspicion of strangling Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in the island's capital city of Naha.
The Yomiuri Shimbun reported that, according to the indictment document, the suspect allegedly strangled the woman from Naha in a hotel with a telephone cord on Oct. 3.
He is also accused of stealing a backpack containing the woman's wallet and other belongings, the newspaper said.
The Marine denied the allegations at the time of his arrest but has now made statements that imply some involvement in the case, the Yomiuri and other media said, citing investigative sources.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by U.S. military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting U.S. troops.
Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi has said that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for U.S. troops in Japan following the alleged killing.
The high-level bilateral consultations will examine off-duty conduct and the "liberty" policy governing off-base private activities of U.S. military personnel, he said.

"We plan to hold discussions including whether the existing rules are effectively functioning," Motegi said, adding that "matters such as patrols and curfew management" would be under review in talks with the United States.

The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by U.S. military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on U.S. military personnel drinking in public off base between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. or going to bars during those hours.
The U.S. military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine's arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew.

Crimes committed by U.S. personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies. The number of arrests related to U.S. service members and their families exceeded 100 last year, according to prefectural police.
Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a U.S. Marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison .
In 2017, a former U.S. Marine and civilian military base worker was sentenced to life in prison for the rape and murder of a local woman in Okinawa.
The same year, U.S. Forces Japan banned all personnel from consuming alcohol after an intoxicated U.S. Marine crashed his vehicle into a mini-truck, killing its 61-year-old local driver.
In Japan, once a suspect is formally indicted, the conviction rate stands at more than 99%.
The justice ministry says the near-perfect rates are because prosecutors only pursue airtight cases, they are confident about winning.
body_zh: 美国海军陆战队因在日本杀害妇女而被指控谋杀罪 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
法院发言人周一告诉法新社，日本检方已起诉一名美国海军陆战队员，罪名是涉嫌在冲绳谋杀一名妇女，该案引发了公众的愤怒。
据称杀害 39 岁日本妇女的事件导致日本首相猛烈抨击这一“令人发指的罪行”，并重新引发了有关美国在日本南部岛屿大量驻军的争议。
那霸法院发言人表示：“此案于10月25日被起诉。”他证实了媒体报道，嫌疑人因谋杀和抢劫罪被起诉。
冲绳县警方表示，他们逮捕了兰斯下士。 20 岁的德文·雅各布·巴拉德 (Devin Jacob Ballard) 驻扎在普天间机场，涉嫌在该岛首府那霸的一家酒店勒死 39 岁的安娜·八木 (Anna Yagi)。
《读卖新闻》报道称，根据起诉书，嫌疑人据称于10月3日在一家酒店内用电话线勒死了那霸市女子。
该报称，他还被指控偷了一个装有该女子钱包和其他物品的背包。
《读卖新闻》和其他媒体援引调查消息人士的话称，这名海军陆战队员在被捕时否认了这些指控，但现在发表了暗示参与此案的声明。
美军人员的强奸、袭击、肇事逃逸和酒后驾驶等犯罪行为长期以来一直在日本南部岛屿引发抗议，多年来该岛一直敦促该国其他地区分担驻扎美军的负担。
日本外务大臣茂木敏充表示，在涉嫌杀戮事件发生后，官员们正在审查驻日美军的基地外行为准则。
他说，高层双边磋商将审查美军人员下班后的行为以及管理美军人员基地外私人活动的“自由”政策。
茂木敏充表示：“我们计划进行讨论，包括现有规则是否有效运作。”他补充说，“巡逻和宵禁管理等问题”将在与美国的谈判中得到审查。
现有政策是在美军人员在冲绳发生一系列性侵犯事件后于 2024 年更新的，其中包括禁止美军人员在凌晨 1 点至 5 点期间在基地外的公共场所饮酒或在这些时间前往酒吧。
这名海军陆战队员被捕后，美国军方暂停了两天的行动，以加强纪律和标准，随后进行了为期一个月的宵禁。
美国人员犯下的罪行一直是这两个亲密安全盟友之间关系的一根刺。据县警方称，去年与美国军人及其家人有关的逮捕人数超过 100 人。
去年，日本一家法院判处一名被指控掐死并试图强奸一名 20 多岁女性的美国海军陆战队员七年监禁。

title_en: What to know about the Israeli elections as Netanyahu faces a battle for survival
title_zh: 内塔尼亚胡面临生存之战，关于以色列选举需要了解什么
summary: After three years of navigating war, crisis and global outcry, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing one of the most significant electoral tests of his decades-long political career.
summary_zh: 经过三年的战争、危机和全球抗议，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡面临着最重要的选举人之一
body_en: Israelis Set to Vote in First Election Since Oct. 7 Attacks

TEL AVIV — After three years of navigating war, crisis and global outcry, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing one of the most significant electoral tests of his decades-long political career.

As Israelis go to the polls on Tuesday, Netanyahu’s party is neck and neck with former Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, who has emerged as his strongest rival in a campaign that has revolved around everything from Israel’s security and military conscription to bread-and-butter issues like the economy.
Crackdown in the West Bank days ahead of Israeli elections
This is the first nationwide election in Israel since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, the deadliest day in the country’s history.

The attacks, which saw 1,195 people killed and 251 taken into Gaza as hostages, triggered a major security crisis that led to three years of war on multiple fronts. There are few households in Israel that haven’t been affected in some way by the events that have played out since, leaving a sense of profound grief and insecurity that lingers across Israeli society.

For most Israelis, the man who has defined the continuing legacy of October 7 is Netanyahu. Many of his opponents believe he has repeatedly evaded responsibility for the intelligence failures leading up to the attacks and what is widely seen as the security forces’ inadequate response.

Bibi, as he’s commonly called, has led Israel for nearly 19 of the past 30 years, with security for many years a core part of his pitch to voters. The 77-year-old has survived political defeats before, only to come back stronger, but a groundswell of opposition could make this one of the most formidable challenges of his political career.

The election is about more than just political survival for Netanyahu — it’s also about his personal freedom. Netanyahu is seeking re-election while also facing long-running criminal cases domestically on charges of fraud, breach of trust and bribery, allegations he has dismissed as a politically motivated witch-hunt.

His grip on power affords him political privileges that have allowed him to drag out those cases, but that could change if he is voted out of power. Critics have derisively accused him of running to stay out of jail.
Netanyahu goes into the election as both the leading candidate and one of the biggest issues dividing voters. His actions before, during and after the Oct. 7 attacks have driven much of the debate.
Netanyahu’s opponents — particularly his strongest rival, Eisenkot, 66 — have rallied around calls for an independent commission of inquiry to investigate the attacks, which Netanyahu has opposed.

Various critics accuse Netanyahu of helping to keep Hamas in power in Gaza in the years before Oct. 7, of prioritizing the fight against Hamas over rescuing Israeli hostages in the wake of the attacks, and of alienating Israel from much of the world with his actions since. Last month, he threatened to sue Israeli newspaper Haaretz over a report that he had been warned about Oct. 7 ahead of time.

“This is the first chance Israelis will have to vote in what is becoming a referendum on what Netanyahu has come to represent following Oct. 7,” said Dahlia Sheindlin, an Israeli American political analyst.

“For his supporters, he is the strong prime minister who fought back and was able to expand the war to other fronts to defend Israel,” she said. “And to his detractors or critics, people supporting parties of the opposition, he’s the prime minister who led to the failures of the government to detect or prevent Oct. 7 and has refused to take accountability for it.”

Netanyahu has staunchly defended his conduct and the war in Gaza, which has left about 74,500 people dead since Oct. 7, according to figures from the Palestinian Ministry of Health. He goes into the election facing an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity, and having vehemently rejected allegations of perpetrating a genocide from a United Nations commission.

But while Israel’s conduct in Gaza has provoked strong international opposition, opinions within Israel remain highly supportive of Israel’s conflicts in Gaza , Lebanon, the West Bank and Iran, with a broad surge in support for right-wing parties and a greater emphasis on Israeli security. Eisenkot, who served in Netanyahu’s war cabinet in the opening months of the war, has criticized strategic failures and supports a long-term ceasefire. He has vowed to remove Hamas from power within 18 months of taking office.

Palestinian-led parties, which largely enjoy support from Palestinian-Israeli citizens who make up 20% of Israel’s population, go into the election as the loudest voices calling for restraint when dealing with Palestinians in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

But Palestinian-Israeli voters in Israel will also cast votes with an eye on the rising scourge of organized crime in their communities that has caused a spike in violent deaths over the past few years.
The vast majority of Palestinians in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip are not Israeli citizens and are not able to vote in the election.
body_zh: 以色列将于 10 月 7 日袭击事件以来首次选举投票
特拉维夫——在经历了三年的战争、危机和全球抗议之后，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡正面临着他数十年政治生涯中最重大的选举考验之一。
随着以色列人周二前往投票站，内塔尼亚胡的政党与前以色列国防军参谋长加迪·艾森科特(Gadi Eisenkot)并驾齐驱，艾森科特在一场围绕以色列安全、征兵和经济等民生问题的竞选活动中成为内塔尼亚胡最强劲的竞争对手。
以色列选举前几天西岸的镇压
这是以色列自 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯领导的袭击以来举行的首次全国选举，这是该国历史上死亡人数最多的一天。
这些袭击导致 1,195 人死亡，251 人被劫持到加沙作为人质，引发了一场重大安全危机，导致多条战线持续三年的战争。在以色列，几乎没有家庭没有受到此后发生的事件的某种影响，以色列社会弥漫着深深的悲伤和不安全感。
对于大多数以色列人来说，定义 10 月 7 日事件持续遗产的人是内塔尼亚胡。他的许多反对者认为，他一再逃避导致袭击的情报失误以及普遍认为安全部队反应不力的责任。
过去 30 年里，人们普遍称呼他为“比比”，他领导以色列近 19 年，多年来，安全一直是他向选民宣传的核心内容。这位 77 岁的老人此前曾经历过政治失败，但后来却变得更加强大，但反对声音的高涨可能使这成为他政治生涯中最艰巨的挑战之一。
这次选举不仅关系到内塔尼亚胡的政治生存，还关系到他的个人自由。内塔尼亚胡正在寻求连任，同时还面临国内长期存在的欺诈、失信和贿赂等刑事案件，他将这些指控斥为出于政治动机的政治迫害。
他对权力的掌控为他提供了政治特权，使他能够拖延这些案件，但如果他被选下台，这种情况可能会改变。批评者嘲笑他竞选是为了逃避牢狱之灾。
内塔尼亚胡作为主要候选人参加选举，也是选民分歧最大的问题之一。他在 10 月 7 日袭击之前、期间和之后的行为引发了很多争论。
内塔尼亚胡的反对者——尤其是他最强劲的竞争对手、66 岁的艾森科特——聚集在一起呼吁成立独立调查委员会来调查这些袭击事件，但内塔尼亚胡对此表示反对。
各种批评人士指责内塔尼亚胡在 10 月 7 日之前的几年里帮助哈马斯在加沙继续掌权，在袭击发生后，他将打击哈马斯的斗争置于营救以色列人质之上，并自此之后的行动疏远了以色列与世界大部分地区的关系。上个月，他威胁要起诉以色列报纸《国土报》，因为有报道称他已提前收到有关 10 月 7 日的警告。
以色列裔美国政治分析人士达丽娅·谢因德林 (Dahlia Sheindlin) 表示，“这是以色列人第一次有机会在 10 月 7 日之后就内塔尼亚胡代表什么问题举行公投”。
“对于他的支持者来说，他是一位强有力的总理，他进行了反击，并能够将战争扩大到其他战线来保卫以色列，”她说。 “对于他的诽谤者或批评者、支持反对党的人来说，他是导致政府未能发现或阻止 10 月 7 日事件的总理，并且拒绝为此承担责任。”
巴勒斯坦卫生部的数据显示，内塔尼亚胡坚决捍卫自己的行为和加沙战争，自 10 月 7 日以来，加沙战争已造成约 74,500 人死亡。他参加选举时面临国际刑事法院以战争罪和反人类罪指控发出的逮捕令，并强烈否认联合国委员会提出的种族灭绝指控。
尽管以色列在加沙的行为激起了国际社会的强烈反对，但以色列内部的舆论仍然高度支持以色列在加沙、黎巴嫩、约旦河西岸和伊朗的冲突，对右翼政党的支持广泛激增，并更加重视以色列的安全。艾森科特在战争开始的几个月内曾在内塔尼亚胡的战时内阁任职，他批评了战略失败并支持长期停火。他发誓要在上任后18个月内将哈马斯赶下台。
巴勒斯坦领导的政党在很大程度上得到了占以色列人口20%的巴勒斯坦-以色列公民的支持，他们在选举中呼吁在处理约旦河西岸和加沙地带的巴勒斯坦人问题时保持克制。
但以色列境内的巴勒斯坦裔以色列选民也将投票关注其社区中日益严重的有组织犯罪祸害，这些犯罪行为导致过去几年暴力死亡人数激增。
约旦河西岸和加沙地带的绝大多数巴勒斯坦人不是以色列公民，无法在选举中投票。

title_en: ‘It’s a mess right now’: RFK’s sweeping changes place new vaccines in limbo
title_zh: “现在一团糟”：RFK 的彻底改变使新疫苗陷入困境
summary: Health secretary’s effort to alter makeup of ACIP panel means no new recommendations coming – even as new vaccines are approved US vaccine recommendations are in limbo, access to vaccines is suffering, and some of the uncertainty may continue for years followi
summary_zh: 卫生部长改变 ACIP 小组构成的努力意味着不会有新的建议出现——即使新疫苗已获得美国疫苗建议的批准
body_en: ‘It’s a mess right now’: RFK’s sweeping changes place new vaccines in limbo
Health secretary’s effort to alter makeup of ACIP panel means no new recommendations coming – even as new vaccines are approved

US vaccine recommendations are in limbo, access to vaccines is suffering, and some of the uncertainty may continue for years following major blows to vaccination by the Trump administration , experts say.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), has made sweeping changes to vaccination policy, cutting childhood immunization recommendations by a third and replacing experts on the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) with his own handpicked allies.

A judge’s order halted these changes because they were not done correctly, but Kennedy has not nominated any new ACIP members – which means there are no new vaccination recommendations coming from the committee, even as new vaccines are approved.
RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau

Ron Kroening, 63, has asthma and bad allergies this time of year, so his doctor recommended the new Moderna mRNA flu vaccine, approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in August for ages 50 and up. Trials suggest it provides even stronger protection than traditional flu shots.
It took time to locate the one pharmacy in his area that stocked the shot – and then Kroening was shocked to be charged a $40 co-pay.

“I figured that was an error because I’ve never had to pay for a flu shot in my life,” he said. But his insurance company told him it’s because there’s no recommendation from the ACIP, Kroening said: “The reason the mRNA isn’t covered is because it’s not listed as an ACIP vaccine.”
If the ACIP doesn’t recommend the new shot by the end of the year – a scenario experts say is likely – insurers won’t be required to cover it until January 2029 at the earliest.

“This is really a barrier. And any barrier to immunizations is going to keep people from getting them,” said Kroening, a retired public health employee who worked on immunizations at the state level in Oklahoma. “A $40 co-pay is going to turn people off,” he added, noting that his pharmacist also didn’t inform him that there were other flu shot options.

Insurers usually have at least a year after FDA approval to add coverage of a new vaccine to their plans, so a co-pay like Kroening’s isn’t unusual in the first year or so. But the difference now is it’s not clear when the vaccine will be fully covered.

Typically, when a vaccine is approved for a new group of people – either because it’s new to the market or because the approval expanded to include more people – insurers have a year from the recommendation to implement it by the next plan year, which usually starts in January. That means if a vaccine is recommended by ACIP in December 2026, insurers are required to cover it by January 2028. If it’s recommended a month later, in January 2027, then the coverage requirement is pushed to January 2029.
“The legal requirement doesn’t go into effect very quickly. The process takes time,” said Lindsay Wiley, professor of law and faculty director of the Health Law and Policy Program at UCLA Law.

For the new flu shot, “it seems likely that at best we would get a recommendation next year,” Wiley said, “but there’s no reason to think” they will do so. “It’s just delaying more and more and more,” she said.

The only exception to the law on coverage is for Covid vaccines, because Congress amended the Affordable Care Act to specifically include coverage of Covid immunizations within 15 days of ACIP recommendation.

The uncertainty around ACIP has other ripple effects. Some states won’t allow pharmacists to give vaccines without an ACIP recommendation. Some of the decisions the committee made before it was disbanded were also halted, including the September 2025 recommendation on new shots to prevent RSV – though insurers appear to be covering them anyway. A now-voided vote to end the universal birth dose of the hepatitis B vaccine is influencing potential state-level laws .
There have also been delays reported for insurers covering the new flu shots for seniors under Medicare, which is mandated by law even without an ACIP recommendation.

The US government has appealed the part of the judge’s order that disbanded the vaccines committee, but there’s nothing to stop Kennedy from undergoing the correct process for appointing new members, experts say. He hasn’t.

“This White House and DoJ are making no serious attempt to actually revive the vaccine committee,” Aaron Siri, who has served as Kennedy’s lawyer and has litigated cases against vaccine makers, wrote on Monday. Siri added: “It appears the DOJ and the White House are doing everything they can to make sure that there is no functioning vaccine committee.”
body_zh: “现在一团糟”：RFK 的彻底改变使新疫苗陷入困境
卫生部长努力改变 ACIP 小组的组成，这意味着即使新疫苗获得批准，也不会提出新的建议
专家表示，美国的疫苗建议悬而未决，疫苗的获取也受到影响，在特朗普政府对疫苗接种进行重大打击后，一些不确定性可能会持续数年。
美国卫生与公共服务部 (HHS) 部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 对疫苗接种政策进行了彻底改变，将儿童免疫建议减少了三分之一，并用他自己精心挑选的盟友取代了免疫实践咨询委员会 (ACIP) 的专家。
法官下令停止这些改变，因为这些改变做得不正确，但肯尼迪没有提名任何新的 ACIP 成员——这意味着即使新疫苗获得批准，委员会也没有提出新的疫苗接种建议。
小罗伯特·肯尼迪的“疫苗研究之神”在几内亚比绍遭到警方突击搜查
63 岁的罗恩·克罗宁 (Ron Kroening) 每年这个时候都会患有哮喘和严重过敏症，因此他的医生推荐了新型 Moderna mRNA 流感疫苗，该疫苗于 8 月获得美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 批准，适用于 50 岁及以上人群。试验表明，它提供比传统流感疫苗更强的保护。
克罗宁花了很长时间才找到了他所在地区储存该疫苗的一家药房，然后克罗宁惊讶地发现自己被收取了 40 美元的自付费用。
“我认为这是一个错误，因为我一生中从未需要为流感疫苗付费，”他说。但他的保险公司告诉他，这是因为 ACIP 没有提出建议，Kroening 说：“mRNA 未被承保的原因是它没有被列为 ACIP 疫苗。”
如果 ACIP 在今年年底前不建议注射新疫苗（专家表示这种情况很可能发生），保险公司最早要到 2029 年 1 月才需要承保。
“这确实是一个障碍。任何免疫接种障碍都会阻止人们获得疫苗，”在俄克拉荷马州从事州级免疫工作的退休公共卫生员工克罗宁说。 “40 美元的共付额会让人们望而却步，”他补充道，并指出他的药剂师也没有告诉他还有其他流感疫苗选择。
保险公司通常在 FDA 批准后至少有一年的时间将新疫苗的承保范围添加到他们的计划中，因此像克罗宁这样的自付费用在第一年左右并不罕见。但现在的不同之处在于，尚不清楚疫苗何时能完全覆盖。
通常情况下，当一种疫苗被批准用于新人群时——要么是因为它是新上市的，要么是因为批准范围扩大到了更多人——保险公司有一年的时间从​​建议到下一个计划年（通常从一月开始）实施该疫苗。这意味着，如果 ACIP 在 2026 年 12 月推荐疫苗，保险公司必须在 2028 年 1 月之前承保。如果一个月后，即 2027 年 1 月推荐疫苗，那么承保要求将推迟到 2029 年 1 月。
“法律要求不会很快生效。这个过程需要时间，”加州大学洛杉矶分校法学院法学教授兼卫生法和政策项目主任林赛·威利 (Lindsay Wiley) 说。
对于新的流感疫苗，“看来我们最多只能在明年得到推荐，”威利说，“但没有理由认为”他们会这样做。 “这只是越来越拖延，”她说。
有关承保范围的法律的唯一例外是 Covid 疫苗，因为国会修订了《平价医疗法案》，明确涵盖 ACIP 建议后 15 天内的 Covid 免疫接种承保范围。
ACIP 的不确定性还会产生其他连锁反应。一些州不允许药剂师在没有 ACIP 建议的情况下提供疫苗。该委员会在解散前做出的一些决定也被暂停，包括 2025 年 9 月关于预防 RSV 的新疫苗的建议——尽管保险公司似乎无论如何都会承保这些决定。一项现已无效的终止乙型肝炎疫苗普遍出生剂量的投票正在影响潜在的州级法律。
据报道，保险公司在医疗保险范围内为老年人提供新的流感疫苗接种也出现了延误，即使没有 ACIP 的建议，医疗保险也是法律规定的。
专家表示，美国政府已对法官命令中解散疫苗委员会的部分提出上诉，但没有什么可以阻止肯尼迪采取正确的程序来任命新成员。他没有。
“白宫和司法部没有认真尝试真正重振疫苗委员会，”曾担任肯尼迪律师并曾对疫苗制造商提起诉讼的亚伦·西里(Aaron Siri)周一写道。 Siri 补充道：“司法部和白宫似乎正在竭尽全力确保疫苗委员会无法正常运作。”

title_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
title_zh: 天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
summary: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump
summary_zh: 两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与天主教徒一起祈祷的照片。
body_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically - ABC News
Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, in a statement titled “A Public Apology,” said Sunday that he had received many questions and comments — some of them distraught — about the meeting on Thursday which he and 11 other bishops attended.
He said the meeting was speedily publicized by the White House with photos and a video, without consent of the participants, and less than two weeks away from the midterm elections .

“I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way," Grob said.
The bishop of Des Moines, Iowa, William Joensen, also issued a statement making clear he felt the White House had taken advantage of the bishops.

“I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose,” he wrote. “I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels.”

Asked whether the White House had or hadn't received the bishop's consent for releasing the photos and video, the press office declined to answer that question. Instead, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers replied, “There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it."

The White House invitation to the bishops — extended in September — offered discussion about such issues as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas , abortion and use of federal tax credits to support private education, according to Joensen and Grob.

“The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party,” wrote Grob. “We were told the meeting was to be a private discussion, that several Catholic members of the cabinet might make an appearance, and that there could be an opportunity to pray privately with the president.”

Airman killed rappelling from Alamodome's ceiling in Salute to Armed Forces ceremony
“It did not take long thereafter for the White House to post a video and photos of the prayer,” Grob said.

“I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election,” he added. “I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family had been harmed by the president’s policies.”
“I did not go without reservations. I wish I had heeded them,” Grob concluded. “I apologize for any damage my actions have done."

Collectively, members of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops have diverse views on Trump and his administration's policies. Minnesota-based Bishop Robert Barron, for example, agreed to serve on Trump's Religious Liberty Commission, which was filled almost entirely with conservative Christians. Some other bishops vehemently denounced aspects of Trump's tough stance on immigration enforcement , saying it runs counter to Catholic teaching.

body_zh: 天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的 - ABC News
天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片
两位天主教主教对同意举行一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片。
密尔沃基大主教杰弗里·格罗布周日在一份题为“公开道歉”的声明中表示，他收到了许多关于他和其他 11 名主教参加的周四会议的问题和评论，其中一些令人心烦意乱。
他表示，白宫在未经与会者同意的情况下，迅速用照片和视频公开了这次会议，而且距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间。
格罗布说：“我感到非常悲伤，不仅因为我造成的痛苦，还因为对一群宗教领袖来说如此神圣的事情，即向我们的天父祈祷，会被以这种方式操纵。”
爱荷华州得梅因主教威廉·约恩森也发表声明，明确表示他认为白宫利用了主教们的利益。
他写道：“我希望自己能更精明一些，不要那么简单，就像那些利用我们的会议来达到党派政治目的的人一样。” “我祈祷自己今后能更加谨慎和明智，尽管我仍然坚定地开放地参与各级政治领导人并为他们祈祷。”
当被问及白宫是否已获得主教同意发布这些照片和视频时，新闻办公室拒绝回答这个问题。相反，白宫发言人泰勒·罗杰斯回答说：“对于美国天主教徒来说，从来没有比特朗普总统更伟大的总统，他的出色记录证明了这一点。”
乔恩森和格罗布表示，白宫于九月延长了对主教的邀请，邀请他们就移民执法、宗教工作者签证、堕胎和利用联邦税收抵免支持私立教育等问题进行讨论。
格罗布写道：“这次会议绝不是对总统、他的政策或他的政党的认可。” “我们被告知，这次会议将是一次私人讨论，几位天主教内阁成员可能会出席，并且可能有机会与总统私下祈祷。”
艾米·阿克顿表示特朗普和万斯在拉马斯瓦米攻击广告后应该“看看事实”
警方称，佛罗里达大学附近发生枪击事件，造成 12 人受伤，其中包括 6 名儿童
飞行员在向武装部队致敬仪式上从阿拉莫圆顶天花板垂降时身亡
“此后不久，白宫就发布了祈祷的视频和照片，”格罗布说。
他补充说：“我很快就开始收到严重关切的信息，担心我可能在全国大选前不到两周的时间里无意中参与了一场政治活动。” “我还听到一些人因为总统政策对他们或他们的家人造成的伤害而感到受伤。”
“我并不是毫无保留地去的。我希望我当时听从了他们的意见，”格罗布总结道。 “对于我的行为造成的任何损害，我深表歉意。”
总的来说，美国天主教主教会议的成员对特朗普及其政府的政策有不同的看法。例如，明尼苏达州的罗伯特·巴伦主教同意在特朗普的宗教自由委员会任职，该委员会几乎全部都是保守派基督徒。其他一些主教强烈谴责特朗普在移民执法方面的强硬立场，称这与天主教教义背道而驰。

title_en: Iowa’s Senate rivals pitch independence from their parties
title_zh: 爱荷华州参议院竞争对手主张独立于其政党
summary: Ashley Hinson qualified her pledge to be Trump’s strongest ally, while Josh Turek praised the president’s border record.
summary_zh: 阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 兑现了自己成为特朗普最强大盟友的承诺，而乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek) 则赞扬了总统的边境记录。
body_en: Republican Ashley Hinson wants Iowans to know she’ll pick a fight with President Donald Trump. Democrat Josh Turek wants them to know he’ll work with him.

The rivals in Iowa’s closely contested Senate race each sought to establish their independence in separate interviews aired Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” pitching themselves as willing to put their state ahead of their respective party loyalty.
Asked about her campaign pledge to be Trump’s “strongest ally” in the Senate, Hinson added a condition: “If it’s for Iowa.”

“I will be someone’s ally when they’re with me on the issues that are important to Iowa,” the Republican lawmaker said. “And if they’re wrong, I’m going to pick a fight with them, no matter who that is.”

The conflicting comments come in a state Trump won by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but where Democrats now see an opportunity to win their first Senate election since 2008. The president campaigned in Iowa this past week as high fuel costs and frustration with his tariffs complicate Republicans’ efforts to maintain the seat.
Republicans close to Hinson told POLITICO last month that she needed to put some distance between herself and Trump, warning that his tariff agenda and the Iran war were undermining her chances.
On Sunday, Hinson rejected Trump’s positive assessment of the economy. “Well, sure doesn’t feel like it right now,” she said, later criticizing the administration’s dealings with Moscow.

“I don’t think we should be making any deals with Russia,” she said, pointing to her vote for sanctions. Her campaign told POLITICO on Friday that she opposed sanctions relief for Russia while supporting Trump’s use of the Defense Production Act to bolster domestic energy production.

But there were limits to her criticism. While calling for the Iran war to end quickly, Hinson declined to oppose a potential new offensive after the midterms, saying she trusted Trump and the military to determine what needed to be done.
Turek, meanwhile, called himself a “proud moderate” and sidestepped a question about whether Democrats had moved too far left.
“I don’t think a lot about the party as a whole. I think about myself, and I think about Iowa,” the Democratic state representative said.

That pitch follows a primary victory aided by national Democratic support , including from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s leadership PAC — which contributed the maximum to Turek’s campaign, though Schumer did not formally endorse. VoteVets spent more than $10 million advertising on Turek’s behalf. He’s also secured the formal endorsement of former President Barack Obama, who appeared in an ad alongside Turek as the two played basketball.

Asked what Trump had done right, Turek said Trump had done “a better job on the border than Biden, for sure.” He also cited agreement on keeping private equity out of housing and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security, while arguing that Trump’s economic policies had concentrated wealth and power.
Also asked whether endorsements mattered, Turek offered a blunt assessment: “Probably not.”
body_zh: 共和党人阿什利·辛森（Ashley Hinson）希望爱荷华州人知道她会与唐纳德·特朗普总统发生争执。民主党人乔什·图雷克希望他们知道他会与他合作。
爱荷华州竞争激烈的参议院竞选中的竞争对手在美国广播公司周日播出的“本周”节目中分别接受采访时，都试图确立自己的独立性，并表示自己愿意将自己的州置于各自政党的忠诚之上。
当被问及她在竞选中承诺成为特朗普在参议院“最强大的盟友”时，辛森补充了一个条件：“如果是为了爱荷华州。”
这位共和党议员说：“当有人在对爱荷华州重要的问题上与我站在一起时，我将成为他们的盟友。” “如果他们错了，我就会和他们打架，不管他们是谁。”
这些相互矛盾的言论出现在特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中以 13 个百分点获胜的州，但民主党现在看到了赢得 2008 年以来首次参议院选举的机会。总统上周在爱荷华州进行竞选活动，因为高昂的燃油成本和对关税的不满使共和党保住席位的努力变得更加复杂。
与辛森关系密切的共和党人上个月告诉《政治》杂志，她需要与特朗普保持一定距离，并警告说，他的关税议程和伊朗战争正在削弱她的机会。
周日，辛森拒绝了特朗普对经济的积极评估。 “嗯，现在肯定不喜欢这样，”她说，后来批评了政府与莫斯科的交往。
“我认为我们不应该与俄罗斯达成任何交易，”她指着自己投票支持制裁说道。她的竞选团队周五告诉《政治》杂志，她反对放松对俄罗斯的制裁，同时支持特朗普利用《国防生产法》来促进国内能源生产。
但她的批评是有限度的。辛森在呼吁迅速结束伊朗战争的同时，拒绝反对中期选举后可能发起的新攻势，并表示她相信特朗普和军方可以决定需要做什么。
与此同时，图雷克称自己是“自豪的温和派”，并回避了民主党是否走得太左的问题。
“我对整个政党的考虑不多。我考虑的是我自己，也考虑的是爱荷华州，”这位民主党州代表说。
这次宣传是在全国民主党的支持下取得初选胜利之后进行的，其中包括参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默领导的政治行动委员会，该组织为图雷克的竞选活动做出了最大贡献，尽管舒默并未正式支持。 VoteVets 为 Turek 花费了超过 1000 万美元的广告费用。他还获得了前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的正式认可，奥巴马在两人打篮球时与图雷克一起出现在广告中。
当被问及特朗普做对了什么时，图雷克表示，特朗普“在边境方面做得比拜登更好”。他还引用了关于阻止私募股权投资住房以及取消小费、加班费和社会保障税的协议，同时认为特朗普的经济政策集中了财富和权力。
当被问及背书是否重要时，图雷克给出了直率的评价：“可能不重要。”

title_en: Court ruling fails to end wait for thousands of immigrants stuck abroad without visas
title_zh: 法院裁决未能结束数千名无签证移民滞留在国外的等待
summary: A federal judge struck down a Trump administration ban on issuing immigrant visas to people from 75 countries, but immigrants continue to be stuck in their countries.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官推翻了特朗普政府向 75 个国家的人发放移民签证的禁令，但移民仍然陷入困境
body_en: Court ruling fails to end wait for thousands of immigrants stuck abroad without visas : NPR

Court ruling fails to end wait for thousands of immigrants stuck abroad without visas A federal judge struck down a Trump administration ban on issuing immigrant visas to people from 75 countries, but immigrants continue to be stuck in their countries.
Court ruling fails to end wait for thousands of immigrants stuck abroad without visas
Gloria and Dustin Hoffman take a selfie with their kids. Gloria Hoffman hide caption
Late last year, Dustin Hoffman and his wife Gloria started the paperwork to secure a visa for her to live in the U.S.

The couple, along with their 5-year-old daughter Chaya and Hoffman's 12-year-old step son Israel, lived together in Argentina, where Hoffman had moved in 2013 after doing a deployment with the U.S. Army in Iraq.

"My daughter is growing up and she's very smart and my stepson he's very smart," Hoffman said. "But the resources in Argentina for an autistic child and the school system in Argentina … I don't know. I just feel like I needed to give my daughter the same opportunities that I had growing up."
New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami
But nearly a year later, the kids and Gloria are stuck in Argentina in bureaucratic limbo due to continuing delays in the processing of their visa.

That's because this January the Trump administration banned the processing of immigrant visas for citizens of 75 countries. Many of the migrants were already in the process of getting a visa. Some already had the visa approved; they were just waiting to get the physical visa delivered to them.
Hoffman's wife is from Colombia, one of the countries on the list.
New report shows the economic toll of ICE raids

A federal judge this August ordered the ban to be lifted, but Hoffman's family still has not gotten their visa, and the State Department continues to ask them to provide additional evidence to prove they have the financial means to live in the U.S. without becoming a public charge.

Attorneys representing migrants say the Hoffman family's case is emblematic of a wider problem: They say the Trump administration is not complying with the federal court order and is instead slow-walking the processing of the visas.

"So while technically the ban doesn't exist, it doesn't matter practically if people are still not being able to get their green card interviews or have their interviews not be finished and not get their immigrant visa stamps foils and be able to come into the United States," said Alexis Axelrad, the president elect of the American Immigration Lawyers Association.
The visa ban affected more than 280,000 immigrants who had applied for visas by the time the policy went into effect in January.

According to an analysis by the libertarian think-tank Cato Institute, the ban targeted thousands of close family members of U.S. citizens and permanent residents, including spouses and minor children. The Cato report called it "one of the most extreme legal immigration policies in U.S. history."
Now stuck in their countries unable to come to the U.S., many are rethinking what to do.

The State Department declined to comment for this story, telling NPR "the matter referenced is subject to pending litigation." On its website , the State Department acknowledges the visa ban is no longer in effect due to the court ruling.
body_zh: 法院裁决未能结束数千名无签证移民滞留在国外的等待：NPR
法院裁决未能结束数千名无签证移民滞留在国外的等待联邦法官推翻了特朗普政府向 75 个国家的人发放移民签证的禁令，但移民仍然被困在自己的国家。
法院裁决未能结束数千名无签证移民滞留在国外的等待
格洛丽亚·霍夫曼 (Gloria Hoffman) 和达斯汀·霍夫曼 (Dustin Hoffman) 与孩子们合影。格洛丽亚霍夫曼隐藏标题栏
去年年底，达斯汀·霍夫曼 (Dustin Hoffman) 和他的妻子格洛丽亚 (Gloria) 开始办理文书工作，为她获得在美国居住的签证。
这对夫妇与他们 5 岁的女儿 Chaya 和霍夫曼 12 岁的继子 Israel 一起住在阿根廷，霍夫曼在伊拉克随美军部署后于 2013 年搬到了阿根廷。
“我的女儿正在长大，她非常聪明，我的继子也非常聪明，”霍夫曼说。 “但是阿根廷为自闭症儿童提供的资源以及阿根廷的学校系统……我不知道。我只是觉得我需要给我的女儿和我成长过程中一样的机会。”
移民法庭的新策略导致迈阿密出现大排长龙和混乱
但近一年后，由于签证处理持续拖延，孩子们和格洛丽亚在阿根廷陷入了官僚主义的困境。
这是因为今年 1 月，特朗普政府禁止为 75 个国家的公民办理移民签证。许多移民已经在申请签证。有些人已经获得签证批准；有些人已经获得签证。他们只是在等待实体签证交付给他们。
霍夫曼的妻子来自名单上的国家之一哥伦比亚。
新报告显示 ICE 突击搜查造成的经济损失
今年八月，一名联邦法官下令解除禁令，但霍夫曼的家人仍未获得签证，国务院继续要求他们提供更多证据，证明他们有经济能力在美国生活而不会成为公共负担。
代表移民的律师表示，霍夫曼家族的案件象征着一个更广泛的问题：他们表示，特朗普政府没有遵守联邦法院的命令，而是在签证处理过程中进展缓慢。
美国移民律师协会当选主席亚历克西斯·阿克塞尔拉德 (Alexis Axelrad) 表示：“因此，虽然从技术上讲，这项禁令并不存在，但实际上，如果人们仍然无法获得绿卡面试，或者面试未完成，无法获得移民签证印章箔并无法进入美国，那实际上并不重要。”
截至一月份该政策生效时，签证禁令影响了超过 28 万申请签证的移民。
根据自由主义智库卡托研究所的分析，该禁令针对的是数千名美国公民和永久居民的近亲，包括配偶和未成年子女。卡托报告称其为“美国历史上最极端的合法移民政策之一”。
现在，许多人被困在自己的国家而无法来美国，他们正在重新考虑该怎么做。
美国国务院拒绝对此事发表评论，并告诉 NPR“所提及的事项尚待审理。”美国国务院在其网站上承认，由于法院的裁决，签证禁令不再有效。

title_en: Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them
title_zh: 共和党花费了数百万美元，但仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区
summary: Republicans redrew Congressional district lines to try to tilt the midterms in their favor. But now they are facing expensive and competitive races they had hoped to outmaneuver.
summary_zh: 共和党人重新划定了国会选区界限，试图让中期选举对他们有利。但现在他们面临着昂贵且竞争激烈的比赛
body_en: Redistricting isn't playing out how Republicans hoped : NPR

Redistricting isn't playing out how Republicans hoped Republicans redrew Congressional district lines to try to tilt the midterms in their favor. But now they are facing expensive and competitive races they had hoped to outmaneuver.
Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them

North Carolina Republican congressional candidates state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom and Laurie Buckhout (right) are embraced by President Trump during an election rally on Oct. 20, 2026, in Greenville, N.C. Buckhout is running in North Carolina's 1st District, which was redrawn to heavily favor Republicans and is now a toss-up. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images hide caption
📲 Get the latest on the midterms & more in the NPR App

Starting last year, President Trump and his political team put pressure on Republican-led states to redraw congressional district lines to favor Republicans. It was supposed to build a firewall for Republicans hoping to avoid the historical pattern of heavy midterm losses for the president's party.
"It just has not turned out that way," said Nathan Gonzales, editor of Inside Elections.
Instead, Republicans are spending millions of dollars on House seats that were supposed to deliver easy wins and may end up losing them anyway.

Among those districts is North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, which the state legislature aggressively redrew late last year to try to make it a reliably Republican district. Under the new lines, Trump would have won the district by more than 11 percentage points in 2024. Now it is widely considered a toss up.
Trump's redistricting gave Republicans a head start, now it goes to the voters
Trump recently headlined a rally in eastern North Carolina where former Republican Party chairman turned U.S. Senate candidate Michael Whatley got most of the attention.
It was cold and getting late when Trump finally got around to mentioning two congressional candidates sitting in the VIP section.

"Come up. The two of you, we have to get them in," Trump said of Laurie Buckout, the Republican nominee in NC-01 and Jennifer Balkcom, the Republican running to represent NC-11 on the opposite side of the state. "We have to vote for them. These are two special people. Come on up."
On stage, Buckhout, a retired Army colonel, who ran and lost in the district two years ago, leaned into the partisan advantage Republicans should have in the district, saying it's "simple math."
"There are more of us," said Buckhout. "All you've got to do is get out the vote. God bless you. Mr. President."

But concern about turnout is exactly why Trump was in the state, begging voters to cast their ballots as if he were on it. Trump told the rally crowd that House Speaker Mike Johnson had asked him to give an extra boost to Buckhout and Balkcom, describing the situation as "tough."
"He said 'if you could, give them a special call out tonight, because they're going to have close races'," Trump said.

Buckhout and her team didn't respond to requests to participate in this story. But, if this redraw was meant to notch an easy Republican win, it hasn't worked out. This is now one of the most expensive House races in the country, with more than $42 million spent on advertising between Sept. 1 and Election Day, according to an NPR analysis of AdImpact data.

body_zh: 重新划分选区并没有如共和党人所希望的那样进行：NPR
选区重新划分并没有体现出共和党人希望共和党人重新划定国会选区界限以试图让中期选举对他们有利的方式。但现在他们面临着昂贵且竞争激烈的比赛，他们原本希望能够以策略取胜。
共和党花费了数百万美元，但仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区
北卡罗来纳州共和党国会候选人表示，2026 年 10 月 20 日，在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔举行的选举集会上，众议员詹妮弗·巴尔克科姆 (Jennifer Balkcom) 和劳里·巴克豪特 (Laurie Buckhout)（右）受到特朗普总统的拥抱。巴克豪特正在北卡罗来纳州第一选区竞选，该选区经过重新划分，严重支持共和党，现在是一个难以预测的局面。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
📲 在 NPR 应用程序中获取有关中期选举的最新动态及更多信息
从去年开始，特朗普总统和他的政治团队向共和党领导的各州施压，要求他们重新划定国会选区界限，以支持共和党。它本应为共和党人建立一道防火墙，希望避免总统所在政党在中期选举中遭受重大损失的历史模式。
“事实并非如此，”《内部选举》编辑内森·冈萨雷斯说。
相反，共和党人花费数百万美元购买众议院席位，这些席位本应轻松获胜，但最终可能会失去这些席位。
这些选区包括北卡罗来纳州第一国会选区，该州立法机构去年年底大力重新划分该选区，试图使其成为一个可靠的共和党选区。根据新的路线，特朗普在 2024 年将以超过 11 个百分点的优势赢得该选区。现在人们普遍认为这是一个胜负难分的事情。
特朗普的选区重新划分给共和党带来了先机，现在轮到选民了
特朗普最近在北卡罗来纳州东部举行了一场集会，前共和党主席、现任美国参议院候选人迈克尔·沃特利 (Michael Whatley) 受到了大部分关注。
当特朗普终于抽出时间提及坐在贵宾区的两位国会候选人时，天气已经很冷了，而且时间已经很晚了。
“上来。你们两个，我们必须让他们进来，”特朗普在谈到 NC-01 的共和党候选人劳里·巴考特 (Laurie Buckout) 和在该州另一边代表 NC-11 竞选的共和党人詹妮弗·巴尔克科姆 (Jennifer Balkcom) 时说道。 “我们必须投票给他们。这是两个特别的人。加油。”
两年前在该选区竞选并落败的退役陆军上校巴克豪特在台上谈到了共和党在该选区应该拥有的党派优势，称这是“简单的数学计算”。
“我们还有更多人，”巴克豪特说。 “你所要做的就是投票。上帝保佑你。总统先生。”
但对投票率的担忧正是特朗普来到该州的原因，他恳求选民像他一样投票。特朗普告诉集会人群，众议院议长迈克·约翰逊要求他为巴克豪特和巴尔科姆提供额外支持，并称形势“艰难”。
特朗普说：“他说，‘如果可以的话，今晚特别呼吁他们，因为他们将进行势均力敌的竞选’。”
巴克豪特和她的团队没有回应参与这篇报道的请求。但是，如果这次重新抽签的目的是让共和党轻松获胜，那么它并没有成功。根据 NPR 对 AdImpact 数据的分析，这是目前美国最昂贵的众议院竞选之一，9 月 1 日至选举日之间的广告支出超过 4200 万美元。
一名志愿者在北卡罗来纳州斯旺斯伯勒的提前投票地点外拍摄了民主党众议员唐·戴维斯 (Don Davis) 与昂斯洛县委员会候选人丽贝卡·库珀 (Rebecca Cooper) 和小米歇尔·利安德烈 (Michel Leandre Jr.) 的合影。昂斯洛是在最新的国会选区界线重新划定中被纳入北卡罗来纳州第一选区的六个县之一。隐藏标题

body_en: Trump attacks El-Sayed over his faith during Michigan rally, calls him "jihadist" - CBS News
President Trump is making his case for Republican candidates in Michigan. He spoke at a rally in Port Huron on Sunday ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

During his speech at McMorran Place, the president said Michigan was built by "American patriots who shed their blood, sweat and tears." He praised Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan , as "one of the most respected men in Washington" and targeted Rogers' Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed.
"I'm here to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator," Mr. Trump said.
CBS News Detroit has reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment on the president's visit and Mr. Trump calling El-Sayed a "jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member," but has yet to hear back.
At a town hall meeting earlier this month in Caro, Michigan, a man asked the U.S. Senate nominee whether he would disavow the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said "absolutely."
Rogers and El-Sayed clashed on Wednesday during their second, and final debate in Southfield, Michigan.
Mr. Trump also voiced support for Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, saying he would "fight for jobs" and "lower prices."

In response to the president's visit, Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said, in part, "By standing with Donald Trump today, Mike Rogers, John James, and Michigan Republicans made it clear they are fully endorsing and ready to rubber stamp Trump's toxic agenda."
On Saturday, former President Barack Obama was in Detroit to drum up support for El-Sayed, Democratic nominee for Michigan governor Jocelyn Benson and other candidates for state office.
El-Sayed appeared at a rally with Sen. Bernie Sanders at the DeVos Performance Hall in Grand Rapids on Sunday evening.
Sanders said Mr. Trump and his allies were using Islamophobia because they have "nothing to say" about the issues most important to working people, such as health care, housing and income inequality.
"All they can do is foment hatred and divisiveness," Sanders said.
Vice President JD Vance is set to stump for Republicans at CHI Aviation in Howell, Michigan, on Tuesday.

特朗普总统正在为密歇根州的共和党候选人阐述自己的观点。周日，他在 11 月 3 日中期选举之前于休伦港举行的一次集会上发表了讲话。
总统在麦克莫兰广场发表讲话时表示，密歇根州是由“流血、汗水和泪水的美国爱国者”建立的。他称赞密歇根州美国参议院共和党候选人迈克·罗杰斯是“华盛顿最受尊敬的人之一”，并把矛头指向了罗杰斯的民主党对手阿卜杜勒·赛义德。
“我来这里是为了阻止圣战穆斯林兄弟会成员成为美国参议员，”特朗普说。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻底特律已联系埃尔赛义德的竞选团队，请其对总统的访问发表评论，特朗普称埃尔赛义德为“圣战穆斯林兄弟会成员”，但尚未收到回复。
本月早些时候在密歇根州卡罗举行的市政厅会议上，一名男子询问美国参议院提名人是否会否认穆斯林兄弟会。埃尔-赛义德说“绝对”。
周三，罗杰斯和埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州南菲尔德举行的第二场也是最后一场辩论中发生了冲突。
特朗普还表示支持共和党州长候选人约翰·詹姆斯，称他将“争取就业机会”和“降低物价”。
作为对总统访问的回应，密歇根州民主党主席柯蒂斯·赫特尔表示，“今天与唐纳德·特朗普站在一起，迈克·罗杰斯、约翰·詹姆斯和密歇根州共和党人明确表示，他们完全支持并准备好盖章特朗普的有毒议程。”
周六，前总统巴拉克·奥巴马 (Barack Obama) 在底特律为密歇根州州长乔斯林·本森 (Jocelyn Benson) 的民主党候选人埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed) 和其他州政府职位候选人争取支持。
周日晚上，埃尔-赛义德与参议员伯尼·桑德斯一起出现在大急流城德沃斯表演厅举行的集会上。
桑德斯表示，特朗普及其盟友之所以利用伊斯兰恐惧症，是因为他们对工薪阶层最重要的问题“无话可说”，例如医疗保健、住房和收入不平等。

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the U.S. would not change his country's positions, after President Trump said Washington "may do another little Epic Fury" — the name used by Washington to describe strikes on Iran when the U.S. and Israel began the war on Feb. 28.

Iran warned on Saturday that U.S. ships would never be allowed in the Persian Gulf "under any circumstances," as tensions between Tehran and Washington continued to mount. Both sides have signaled a possible return to strikes.

U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Friday that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad, with plots to kill Americans reaching "advanced stages" in the Middle East and other countries.
3:25 AM Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan to hold talks with Iran Monday in Tehran, officials say
Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan will hold talks on regional security with Iranian officials on Monday in Tehran, Iranian and Saudi authorities said.
The meeting would follow eight months of war in the Middle East and recent U.S. and Israeli threats of renewed attacks against Iran.

"As agreed, Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will participate in this meeting," said Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council.
In an interview with state television, Kani said the meeting will also include Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei.
Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Dr Rayed Krimly confirmed that the kingdom's defense minister was heading a delegation to Tehran on Monday.
"The visit comes as part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement countries for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis," Krimly said in a post on X.
It is aimed at "promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by the State of Qatar and the Islamic Republic of Pakistan," he added.

The Saudi-led military coalition said Monday it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen's Houthis, after the Iran-backed group claimed a new attack on the international airport in Riyadh.

A Houthis spokesperson said they launched attacks the airport on Sunday , just hours after it resumed flights. Deadly strikes by the rebel group earlier this month had forced the airport to shut down operations for more than two weeks .

Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said on Monday that air defenses "intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile" fired by the Houthis toward Riyadh and destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Yemen's capital Sanaa.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Monday the group "successfully targeted" the airport with a ballistic missile, and struck oil pumping stations with drones.

title_en: Peltola postpones campaign stops after Saturday car crash
title_zh: 佩尔托拉在周六车祸后推迟了竞选活动
summary: The Alaska Senate candidate and her family sustained minor injuries, her campaign announced Sunday.
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加州参议员候选人及其家人受轻伤，她的竞选团队周日宣布。
body_en: Former Rep. Mary Peltola is postponing campaign stops in her bid for Alaska’s Senate seat after she and her family sustained minor injuries in a car crash Saturday night.
Peltola and her family were traveling to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet when another driver struck their vehicle, her campaign announced Sunday on social media.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in the statement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”

Anchorage police said a vehicle rear-ended the car carrying Peltola at a red light Saturday evening, pushing it into a third vehicle. Peltola and the other passengers of her car were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
The driver who struck their vehicle was also hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Police said the crash remains under investigation.

The crash disrupts the start of Peltola’s eight-community “Alaska Always Tour,” a seven-day campaign swing ahead of the midterms. Events in Fairbanks and Bethel originally scheduled for Sunday and Monday will be rescheduled, while stops in Homer, Kenai, Seward, Juneau, Anchorage and Palmer will continue as planned, the campaign said.
The midterm elections are just over a week away.
Peltola, a Democrat, is challenging Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in a closely watched race that could help determine control of the Senate.

The race on Thursday became the subject of a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the election results if Sullivan loses in November. The administration is arguing that the presence of an independent candidate also named Dan Sullivan is an effort to mislead voters, despite the Alaska Supreme Court allowing the other Sullivan to remain on the ballot in a June ruling.

Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the lawsuit Sunday, arguing that voters could confuse the two candidates. Peltola’s campaign called the suit a “despicable political threat to overturn the election.” Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) piled on, saying the Justice Department's suit should never have been filed.

Alaska’s political history has been marked by fatal transportation disasters. Peltola’s husband, Eugene “Buzzy” Peltola Jr., died in September 2023 when the small plane he was piloting crashed after takeoff in southwestern Alaska. Former Republican Sen. Ted Stevens died in a plane crash in 2010 near Dillingham, and Democratic Rep. Nick Begich disappeared in 1972 after disembarking from Anchorage on a small plane traveling to Juneau.
body_zh: 前众议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）和她的家人在周六晚上的一场车祸中受了轻伤，她正在推迟竞选阿拉斯加州参议员席位的竞选活动。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队周日在社交媒体上宣布，当时佩尔托拉和她的家人正在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会的年度宴会，另一名司机撞上了他们的车辆。
竞选经理谢丽尔·布鲁斯在声明中表示：“玛丽和她的家人受了轻伤，但精神状态良好。” “不幸的是，根据医疗专业人士的建议，玛丽即将在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将被重新安排在本周晚些时候，因为她需要时间来康复。”
安克雷奇警方表示，周六晚上红灯时，一辆汽车追尾了载有佩尔托拉的汽车，将其撞向第三辆车。警方称，佩尔托拉和车上的其他乘客被送往当地一家医院，伤势没有生命危险。
撞上车辆的司机也被送往医院，没有生命危险。警方表示，事故仍在调查中。
这次事故扰乱了佩尔托拉八个社区的“阿拉斯加永远之旅”的开始，这是中期选举前为期 7 天的竞选活动。该活动表示，原定于周日和周一在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将重新安排，而在荷马、基奈、苏厄德、朱诺、安克雷奇和帕尔默的活动将按计划继续进行。
距离中期选举只剩一周多了。
民主党人佩尔托拉正在一场备受关注的竞选中挑战共和党参议员丹·沙利文，这场竞选可能有助于确定参议院​​的控制权。
周四的竞选成为司法部诉讼的主题，如果沙利文在 11 月失败，司法部将阻止对选举结果的认证。政府认为，尽管阿拉斯加最高法院在六月的裁决中允许另一位沙利文继续留在选票上，但一位也叫丹·沙利文的独立候选人的出现是在误导选民。
司法部长托德·布兰奇周日为这起诉讼进行了辩护，称选民可能会混淆两位候选人。佩尔托拉的竞选团队称该诉讼是“推翻选举的卑鄙政治威胁”。共和党参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基（阿拉斯加州共和党人）继续说道，司法部根本不应该提起诉讼。

阿拉斯加的政治历史以致命的交通灾难为标志。佩尔托拉的丈夫小尤金·“巴兹”·佩尔托拉于 2023 年 9 月去世，当时他驾驶的小型飞机在阿拉斯加西南部起飞后坠毁。前共和党参议员特德·史蒂文斯 (Ted Stevens) 于 2010 年在迪林厄姆 (Dillingham) 附近的一次飞机失事中丧生，民主党众议员尼克·贝吉奇 (Nick Begich) 于 1972 年乘坐一架飞往朱诺的小型飞机从安克雷奇下飞机后失踪。

title_en: Trump leans into Islamophobic rhetoric at Michigan rally
title_zh: 特朗普在密歇根集会上倾向于仇视伊斯兰教的言论
summary: The president attacked Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat against Republican Mike Rogers.
summary_zh: 总统攻击了民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德，他与共和党人迈克·罗杰斯陷入了胶着状态。
body_en: Trump and Obama rally supporters in key battleground states ahead of midterms

President Donald Trump embraced Islamophobic rhetoric Sunday as he rallied in Port Huron, Michigan, in support of the state’s Republican candidates, including the GOP Senate nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers.

Trump alleged that Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat with Rogers, is a “jihadist,” calling him a “Muslim Brotherhood member” while saying Rogers is “apple pie.”

“Anyone with that record of support for jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate,” Trump said about El-Sayed.
Throughout his comments Sunday, Trump offered no evidence for any of the claims about El-Sayed.
“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector,” Trump said.

Trump sought to draw a comparison between the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks and El-Sayed as he introduced speaker David Beamer, whose son, Todd Beamer, was a passenger who died on the hijacked United Flight 93.
“Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight just like Todd did to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” Trump said.
Beamer went on to extend Trump’s comparison between the Senate race and 9/11.

“What has changed? Well, one thing is 9/11 was a surprise attack. What’s going on right now in our country and here in Michigan? It’s not a surprise. We can see the attack coming that culminates in this battleground state on Tuesday, November the 3rd,” Beamer said as Trump stood behind him onstage.
“What’s different this time is the enemy has not come from abroad. The enemy is right here among us, local terrorists, local citizens that want to demolish our country,” he added.
Beamer, who has been featured in Rogers’ campaign ads, compared the two men and claimed Rogers is “an American” while saying El-Sayed is not, going on to call him “anti-American.”
“Abdul has a birth certificate. The birth certificate says he’s a citizen of America. You know what? A birth certificate doesn’t make you an American,” Beamer said.
“He has blood that’s red. However, he has chosen to remove any strain of the white and blue part in his life. We cannot, cannot allow this man to invade and occupy our country,” he added.
Both Rogers and El-Sayed were born in Michigan.
El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump’s and Beamer’s remarks.
El-Sayed went viral for a heated interaction last week with a town hall attendee who asked him to condemn the organization.
“You assume ... that because I am Muslim that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed told the attendee last week.

Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. The Trump administration has designated certain chapters of the group in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt as terrorist organizations. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied any ties to the group, which he has denounced.

Rogers was asked Sunday about Trump’s calling El-Sayed a “Muslim Brotherhood jihadist” and a “violent terrorist” in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press.” Pressed about whether he agreed with Trump’s characterizations, Rogers said the election is about “me versus Abdul,” adding, “I’ve never called him a terrorist.”
body_zh: 中期选举前，特朗普和奥巴马在关键战场州集结支持者
唐纳德·特朗普总统周日在密歇根州休伦港集会时发表了仇视伊斯兰教的言论，支持该州的共和党候选人，其中包括共和党参议院候选人、前众议员迈克·罗杰斯。
特朗普声称与罗杰斯不和的民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德是一名“圣战分子”，称他为“穆斯林兄弟会成员”，同时称罗杰斯是“苹果派”。
“任何有支持圣战分子记录的人都会受到筛查，并且无法在飞机上找到座位。他们当然不应该给他在美国参议院的席位，”特朗普谈到埃尔-赛义德时说道。 “他将是唯一一位在被允许进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器的参议员。我希望他有一个金属探测器。”
在周日的讲话中，特朗普没有提供任何证据来证明有关埃尔赛义德的任何说法。
“他将是唯一一位在被允许进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器的参议员。我希望他有一个金属探测器，”特朗普说。
特朗普在介绍议长戴维·比默时试图将 2001 年 9 月 11 日的袭击事件与埃尔·赛义德进行比较。比默的儿子托德·比默是在被劫持的美联航 93 号航班上丧生的乘客。
特朗普说：“二十五年后，密歇根州需要像托德那样站起来并战斗，阻止圣战分子走进国会大厦。”
比默继续将特朗普的参议院竞选与 9/11 进行比较。
“发生了什么变化？嗯，有一点是，9/11 是一次突然袭击。我们国家和密歇根州现在正在发生什么？这并不奇怪。我们可以看到袭击即将到来，并在 11 月 3 日星期二在这个战场州达到顶峰，”特朗普在台上站在他身后时，比默说道。
“这次不同的是，敌人不是来自国外。敌人就在我们中间，是当地的恐怖分子，是想要摧毁我们国家的当地公民，”他补充道。
曾出现在罗杰斯竞选广告中的比默将这两个人进行了比较，并声称罗杰斯是“美国人”，而埃尔赛义德则不是，并称他为“反美国人”。
“阿卜杜勒有出生证明。出生证明上说他是美国公民。你知道吗？出生证明并不意味着你就是美国人，”比默说。
“他的血液是红色的。然而，他选择消除生命中白色和蓝色部分的任何张力。我们不能、不能允许这个人入侵和占领我们的国家，”他补充道。
罗杰斯和埃尔-赛义德都出生于密歇根州。
赛义德的竞选团队没有立即回应对特朗普和比默言论发表评论的请求。
上周，埃尔-赛义德因与一名市政厅与会者的激烈互动而走红，与会者要求他谴责该组织。
“你认为……因为我是穆斯林，所以我会以某种方式效忠一些不属于我们宪法的东西，”赛义德上周告诉与会者。
特朗普指责埃尔-赛义德与穆斯林兄弟会有联系，穆斯林兄弟会是一个 1928 年在埃及成立的国际逊尼派伊斯兰组织。特朗普政府已将该组织在黎巴嫩、约旦和埃及的某些分会指定为恐怖组织。埃尔-赛义德一再否认与该组织有任何关系，并对此予以谴责。
周日，罗杰斯在接受美国全国广播公司(NBC)“会见媒体”节目时被问及特朗普称埃尔-赛义德为“穆斯林兄弟会圣战分子”和“暴力恐怖分子”一事。当被问及他是否同意特朗普的描述时，罗杰斯表示，这次选举是关于“我与阿卜杜勒”的斗争，并补充说，“我从未称他为恐怖分子。”

title_en: Scoop: Netanyahu presses Trump for more support ahead of tight Tuesday election
title_zh: 独家新闻：内塔尼亚胡在周二紧张的选举之前向特朗普施压，要求他提供更多支持
summary: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — fighting for political survival in Tuesday's elections — has pleaded with President Trump in recent days to show more public support for his campaign, according to a U.S. source with knowledge and
summary_zh: 以色列特拉维夫 — 以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡 — 在周二的选举中为政治生存而奋斗 — 向特鲁总统恳求
body_en: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — fighting for political survival in Tuesday's elections — has pleaded with President Trump in recent days to show more public support for his campaign, according to a U.S. source with knowledge and an Israeli source briefed on the matter.
Why it matters: The U.S. source said the White House sees Netanyahu's aggressive lobbying as a "sign of desperation" and an indication that the Israeli leader thinks he's trailing.
Neta Molcho, a spokesperson for Netanyahu's Likud party, denied the prime minister asked Trump to support his campaign "in recent days or before his endorsement statement."
The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Trump said in an interview with Newsmax two weeks ago that people in Israel asked him to get involved in support of Netanyahu.
Behind the scenes: The U.S. source said Netanyahu spoke with Trump twice in the last three days and asked him to double down on his Truth Social post last week endorsing him.
The source said Netanyahu even suggested language for additional statements of support.
An Israeli source briefed on Netanyahu's efforts said the Israeli prime minister proposed that Trump hold calls with Israeli reporters to express further support.
Driving the news: After weeks of hesitation, Trump endorsed Netanyahu last Sunday. He went as far as to suggest his defeat would have consequences for U.S.-Israel relations.
Trump has never worked with an Israeli prime minister other than Netanyahu, and he doesn't personally know any of the other candidates. The two have forged a close but often turbulent relationship.
State of play: Three major Israeli television networks released their final pre-election polls Friday, all showing Netanyahu's coalition falling well short of a parliamentary majority.

All three projected just 50 seats for Netanyahu's bloc in the 120-member Knesset — 17 fewer than his current coalition holds. His Likud party, which currently holds 32 seats, was projected to win just 20.

The polls gave former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc between 52 and 56 seats, with another 14–16 going to two Arab Israeli parties. Channel 11 also projected four seats for a reservists party unaffiliated with either bloc.
Pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 was the major outlier, projecting 60 seats for his bloc and 30 for Likud in a poll earlier this week.
Between the lines: One U.S. official described the endorsement as a win-win for Trump, regardless of the outcome.
If Netanyahu wins — or remains in power as a caretaker prime minister — Trump could claim credit for rescuing him politically and use that leverage to press for concessions.

If Netanyahu loses and his opponents form a government, Israel's new leaders would still have every incentive to cultivate good relations with Trump. His endorsement of their rival would quickly become a footnote.
Yes, but: Some of Trump's advisers see opportunity for his Middle East agenda in an Israeli government led by someone else.
body_zh: 以色列特拉维夫——据一位知情的美国消息人士和一位了解情况的以色列消息人士透露，在周二的选举中为政治生存而奋斗的以色列总理本雅明内塔尼亚胡最近几天恳求特朗普总统对他的竞选活动表现出更多的公众支持。
为什么重要：美国消息人士称，白宫将内塔尼亚胡积极的游说视为“绝望的迹象”，并表明这位以色列领导人认为他正在落后。
内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团发言人内塔·莫尔乔否认总理“在最近几天或在发表背书声明之前”要求特朗普支持他的竞选活动。
白宫没有回应置评请求。特朗普两周前接受Newsmax采访时表示，以色列民众要求他参与支持内塔尼亚胡。
幕后花絮：美国消息人士称，内塔尼亚胡在过去三天内与特朗普两次通话，并要求他加大上周在《真相社会》帖子上对他的支持。
消息人士称，内塔尼亚胡甚至建议使用额外的支持声明。
一位了解内塔尼亚胡努力的以色列消息人士称，以色列总理提议特朗普与以色列记者通话以表达进一步的支持。
推动新闻：经过数周的犹豫之后，特朗普于上周日支持了内塔尼亚胡。他甚至暗示他的失败将对美以关系产生影响。
除了内塔尼亚胡之外，特朗普从未与以色列总理合作过，他个人也不认识任何其他候选人。两人建立了密切但经常动荡的关系。
现状：以色列三大电视网络周五公布了最终的选举前民意调查，所有民意调查均显示内塔尼亚胡的联盟远未获得议会多数席位。
三人都预测内塔尼亚胡的集团在议会 120 名成员中仅获得 50 个席位，比他目前的联盟所拥有的席位少 17 个。他的利库德集团目前拥有 32 个席位，预计只会赢得 20 个席位。
民意调查显示，前军事首领加迪·艾森科特的反对党集团获得了 52 至 56 个席位，另外两个阿拉伯以色列政党获得了 14 比 16 的席位。 Channel 11 还为与任何一个集团都无关的预备役政党安排了四个席位。
支持内塔尼亚胡的 Channel 14 是一个主要的异常值，在本周早些时候的一项民意调查中，预计他的集团将获得 60 个席位，利库德集团将获得 30 个席位。
言外之意是：一位美国官员称，无论结果如何，对特朗普的支持都是双赢。
如果内塔尼亚胡获胜——或者作为看守总理继续掌权——特朗普可能会因在政治上拯救他而获得赞誉，并利用这一影响力迫使他让步。
如果内塔尼亚胡失败并且他的对手组建政府，以色列新领导人仍然有充分的动力与特朗普建立良好关系。他对对手的支持很快就成为一个脚注。
是的，但是：特朗普的一些顾问在由其他人领导的以色列政府中看到了他的中东议程的机会。

Eric Bauza, voice actor for the modern-day Bugs Bunny, dies at 46
Eric Bauza, best known for voicing the lovable “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died, his family said Monday.
Bauza’s family issued a brief statement on his official Instagram page stating that he had “passed away suddenly,” without giving further details.
The Emmy Award-winning voice actor was the “modern voice of iconic “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters,” the statement said.
Bauza died Sunday at his residence, according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office, which noted that he had been diagnosed with hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
“Eric was a unique and versatile voice actor who was loved by everyone he knew and worked with,” his manager, Judy Coppage, told NBC News by email.

“His sudden passing is a shock to all of us, and he will be deeply missed. It’s a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and his fans,” Coppage added. “The pleasure of watching him succeed and excel to become one of the most accomplished voices in animation was rewarding and thrilling.”
The Canadian-American won three Emmy awards between 2022 and 2025 for his work, including voicing characters such as Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian and Tweety.

He was also the first person of color to voice Bugs Bunny in the “Looney Tunes” cartoons, which he told NBC News in a 2021 interview led to a deluge of encouragement and adoration from the Asian American community.
“Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures,” he said at the time. “It doesn’t matter what part of the planet you’re from. You get the comedy.”

Bauza said he grew up a massive ”Looney Tunes” fan, noting that the classic cartoons were part of the bond between his Filipino immigrant father and grandfather. He also said his obsessive attention to detail and persistence formed the foundation of his craft, as he grew up mimicking cartoon voices.

Bauza also voiced some of the biggest animated characters in the 2021 movie “Space Jam: A New Legacy” and appeared in the 2023 “Super Mario Bros. Movie” and, most recently, the 2026 “Coyote vs. Acme” film.

He also lent his voice to characters including Stimpy Cat in “Ren & Stimpy,” Foop from “The Fairly OddParents,” Fozzie Bear from “Muppet Babies” and the Beagle Boys from “DuckTales,” according to his IMDb page.
Adela Suliman is a breaking-news editor and reporter for NBC News in London.

埃里克·鲍扎 (Eric Bauza) 因为可爱的《乐一通》角色兔八哥、达菲鸭和小猪配音而闻名，他的家人周一表示，他已经去世。
巴乌扎的家人在他的 Instagram 官方页面上发表了一份简短声明，称他“突然去世”，但没有透露更多细节。
声明称，这位艾美奖获奖配音演员是“兔八哥和达菲鸭以及其他数十个深受喜爱的卡通人物的现代配音”。
据洛杉矶县法医办公室称，鲍扎周日在他的住所去世，并指出他被诊断患有高血压心血管疾病。
“埃里克是一位独特且多才多艺的配音演员，他受到所有认识和共事过的人的喜爱，”他的经纪人朱迪·科佩奇通过电子邮件告诉 NBC 新闻。
“他的突然去世让我们所有人感到震惊，我们将深深怀念他。这对他的家人、动画行业和粉丝来说都是巨大的损失，”科佩奇补充道。 “看到他成功并成为动画界最有成就的声音之一，我感到很高兴，也很兴奋。”
这位加拿大裔美国人因其作品在 2022 年至 2025 年间赢得了三项艾美奖，其中包括为埃尔默·福德、火星人马文和崔弟等角色配音。
他也是第一个在《乐一通》卡通片中为兔八哥配音的有色人种，他在 2021 年接受 NBC 新闻采访时表示，这引起了亚裔美国人社区的大量鼓励和崇拜。
“乐一通超越了所有语言和所有文化，”他当时说道。 “无论你来自地球的哪个地方，你都会看到喜剧。”
鲍扎说，他从小就是《乐一通》的忠实粉丝，并指出这些经典动画片是他的菲律宾移民父亲和祖父之间纽带的一部分。他还说，他对细节的痴迷和坚持构成了他的技艺的基础，因为他是模仿卡通声音长大的。
Bauza 还在 2021 年电影《太空大灌篮：新遗产》中为一些最知名的动画角色配音，并出现在 2023 年《超级马里奥兄弟电影》和最近的 2026 年电影《狼大战阿克米》中。
根据他的 IMDb 页面，他还为《Ren & Stimpy》中的 Stimpy Cat、《The Fairly OddParents》中的 Foop、《Muppet Babies》中的 Fozzie Bear 以及《DuckTales》中的 Beagle Boys 等角色配音。
阿德拉·苏利曼 (Adela Suliman) 是 NBC 新闻驻伦敦的突发新闻编辑兼记者。

title_en: Only the shaky Vikings are undefeated after depleted 49ers lose and Chiefs get dominated
title_zh: 在精疲力尽的 49 人队输球、酋长队占据统治地位之后，只有摇摇欲坠的维京人队保持不败
summary: Brock Purdy and the 49ers couldn’t overcome all the injuries one more time
summary_zh: 布洛克·珀迪和 49 人队无法再次克服所有伤病
body_en: Only the shaky Vikings are undefeated after depleted 49ers lose and Chiefs get dominated
Brock Purdy and the 49ers couldn’t overcome all the injuries one more time
Brock Purdy and the 49ers couldn’t overcome all the injuries one more time. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs ran into the defending Super Bowl champions and their stingy defense.
Only the Minnesota Vikings remain unbeaten — for now — and they battled to beat the Colts.

Sunday kicked off with Aaron Rodgers leading the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first regular-season game in France. It ended with the Seahawks shutting down Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs in Seattle in a 20-3 victory.

Despite a slew of injuries, San Francisco opened the season 6-0. But the 49ers wasted a 14-3 lead in a 29-20 loss at Atlanta. The Niners didn’t have their top five receivers, including Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. They lost Christian McCaffrey for part of the game. Still, they had the ball and an opportunity to drive for the go-ahead score until Purdy threw his second interception near midfield down by six with under three minutes left. The Falcons scored 13 points on San Francisco’s four turnovers.

“We had the momentum, we were moving the ball well, I feel like we were running the ball really well offensively and then all of the sudden it’s like a couple plays make you feel like dang, we’re not doing our job,” Purdy said. “Obviously, the most important thing is protecting the football. That’s really the number one thing in our organization as an offense. … and so when you do have those kind of costly mistakes, it does make you feel like all right we’re not doing anything, we’re not putting up points like we need to. It starts with me at quarterback and I think it bleeds into everybody else, too.”
The Niners get a week off to rest and recover before hosting Las Vegas (3-4) on Nov. 8.
The Chiefs (5-1) already had their bye week so they have to fix their problems quickly with a matchup for first place in the AFC West coming up next Sunday at Denver (5-2).

Seattle’s “Dark Side" defense held Walker to 36 yards rushing on 14 carries in his first game against his former team. The Super Bowl MVP entered Week 7 leading the NFL in rushing and had four 100-yard games in the first five.
Mahomes only completed 57.6% of his passes and didn’t guide Kansas City’s offense into the red zone for the first time in his career.
“You don’t want to perform like this in prime time in a big moment like this,” Mahomes said.
So the Vikings (6-0) are the last undefeated team in the league. But they need to improve a shaky offense to stay perfect.
Minnesota rallied for a 16-10 victory over Indianapolis thanks to another stellar effort from the defense, which held the Colts to just 218 yards.

Airman killed rappelling from Alamodome's ceiling in Salute to Armed Forces ceremony
Kyler Murray threw for 150 yards and the Vikings had just 275 total yards.

“You can’t get down on it right now, just because it’s still relatively early enough that we’re catching our stride,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said. “But at the same time, we know, with the type of teams that are going to be on our schedule the rest of the way and where we want to go with this team, we’ll keep progressing.”

The Vikings have a difficult stretch coming up. They visit the Lions (4-2) next week, host the Bills (5-1) and then face the Packers (4-3) and 49ers in back-to-back games on the road. They need more production on offense to stay on top in a tough NFC North that includes four teams with a winning record.
body_zh: 在精疲力尽的 49 人队输球、酋长队占据统治地位之后，只有摇摇欲坠的维京人队保持不败
布洛克·珀迪和 49 人队无法再次克服所有伤病
布洛克·珀迪和 49 人队无法再一次克服所有的伤病。帕特里克·马霍姆斯和酋长队遭遇了超级碗卫冕冠军及其吝啬的防守。
目前，只有明尼苏达维京人队保持不败，他们正在为击败小马队而战。
周日，亚伦·罗杰斯带领匹兹堡钢人队以 16-10 战胜新奥尔良圣徒队，这是 NFL 在法国举行的首场常规赛。最终海鹰队在西雅图击败了马霍姆斯、肯尼思·沃克三世和酋长队，以 20-3 获胜。
尽管伤病不断，旧金山队仍以 6-0 开局。但49人队以29-20输给亚特兰大队，浪费了14-3的领先优势。九人队没有包括迈克·埃文斯和迪博·塞缪尔在内的前五名接球手。他们在部分比赛中失去了克里斯蒂安·麦卡弗里。尽管如此，他们仍然拥有球权，并且有机会突破比分，直到珀迪在中场附近的第二次拦截在比赛还剩不到三分钟时将比分落后六分。猎鹰队在旧金山队的四次失误中拿下 13 分。
“我们有动力，我们很好地转移了球，我觉得我们在进攻上跑球非常好，然后突然之间，就像有几场比赛让你感觉很糟糕，我们没有做好我们的工作，”珀迪说。 “显然，最重要的事情是保护足球。这确实是我们组织中进攻的第一件事。......所以当你确实犯了这种代价高昂的错误时，它确实会让你觉得我们什么都没做，我们没有像我们需要的那样得分。这从我作为四分卫开始，我认为它也会渗透到其他每个人身上。”
九人队在 11 月 8 日主场迎战拉斯维加斯（3-4）之前休息一周。
酋长队 (5-1) 已经度过了轮空周，因此他们必须尽快解决问题，下周日将在丹佛 (5-2) 进行亚冠西部第一名的对决。
西雅图队的“黑暗面”防守让沃克在对阵老东家的第一场比赛中冲球 14 码，冲球距离只有 36 码。这位超级碗 MVP 进入了第七周，在冲球方面领先 NFL，并在前五场比赛中有四场 100 码比赛。
马霍姆斯的传球成功率只有57.6%，职业生涯第一次没有引导堪萨斯城的进攻进入红区。
“你不想在这样的重要时刻在黄金时段表现得这样，”马霍姆斯说。
所以维京人队（6胜0负）是联盟最后一支不败球队。但他们需要改进不稳定的进攻才能保持完美。
明尼苏达州队以 16-10 战胜印第安纳波利斯队，这要归功于防守组的又一次出色表现，将小马队的距离限制在 218 码。

飞行员在向武装部队致敬仪式上从阿拉莫圆顶天花板垂降时身亡
凯勒·穆雷 (Kyler Murray) 传球推进了 150 码，而维京人队的总传球码数仅为 275 码。
维京人队教练凯文·奥康奈尔说：“你现在不能掉以轻心，因为现在还相对较早，我们正在追赶我们的步伐。” “但与此同时，我们知道，根据剩下的时间安排中的球队类型以及我们希望与这支球队一起去的地方，我们将继续进步。”
维京人接下来将面临一段艰难的时期。下周他们将客场挑战雄狮队 (4-2)，主场迎战比尔队 (5-1)，然后在客场背靠背对阵包装工队 (4-3) 和 49 人队。他们需要在进攻上做出更多贡献，才能在艰难的国联北部地区保持领先地位，其中包括四支拥有获胜记录的球队。

body_en: Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida - ABC News
Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
President Donald Trump has cast his ballot in the midterm elections, voting for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally
By JOSH BOAK Associated Press and JILL COLVIN Associated Press
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday, saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally.

Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office together after the president spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has been criticized in the past for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.
Asked if he voted the party line, Trump, who was wearing an “I Voted” sticker, said, “Very much so.”

Speaking to reporters at the poll site, Trump again defended an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy . The ad has faced intense blowback for featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton, who lost custody of her children after her husband, the children’s stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.

Trump also defended his decision to instruct his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses over the inclusion of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
As for the war in Iran, he said, “I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they’ll make a deal, but I’m not sure. Either way, we win.”

Melania Trump , who this week brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid could be delivered and civilians evacuated, was asked whether she might travel to Ukraine.

乔什·博克 (JOSH BOAK) 美联社和吉尔·科尔文 (JILL COLVIN) 美联社
佛罗里达州西棕榈滩——唐纳德·特朗普总统周六在中期选举中投票，他在佐治亚州集会上发表讲话之前表示，他投票给了佛罗里达州的所有共和党人。
总统在附近的高尔夫球场度过了一个上午后，特朗普和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普一起抵达棕榈滩县选举监督办公室的西棕榈滩投票站。特朗普过去因邮寄投票而受到批评，尽管他长期以来一直反对这种提交选票的方法。
当被问及是否投票支持党派路线时，戴着“我投票”贴纸的特朗普说：“非常喜欢。”
特朗普在投票站对记者发表讲话，再次为俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米的广告辩护。该广告因以民主党竞争对手艾米·阿克顿博士的疏远母亲为主角而面临强烈反弹。艾米·阿克顿博士的丈夫，即孩子们的继父，因在她 12 岁时强奸阿克顿而被起诉，从而失去了孩子们的监护权。
特朗普还为自己的决定进行了辩护，即如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文因将第二位名叫丹·沙利文的候选人纳入选票而失败，他将指示他的政府提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。
至于伊朗战争，他说，“我可能必须结束它。或者也许他们会达成协议，但我不确定。无论哪种方式，我们都会赢。”
梅拉尼娅·特朗普本周在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市奥列什基促成了俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的停火，以便能够提供人道主义援助并疏散平民。有人问她是否可能前往乌克兰。

title_en: Woman, 93, outwits scammer, helps get him arrested, police say
title_zh: 警方称，93岁女子智胜骗子，帮助他被捕
summary: A 93-year-old woman in western Japan outsmarted a suspected scammer by pretending to fall for the scheme and helping police arrest him at her home, an officer said.
summary_zh: 日本西部的一名 93 岁妇女假装落入诈骗团伙，并帮助警方在她家中将其逮捕，从而智胜了一名诈骗嫌疑人。
body_en: Woman, 93, outwits would-be scammer, helps get him arrested, police say - CBS News
A 93-year-old woman in western Japan outsmarted a suspected scammer by pretending to fall for the scheme and helping police arrest him at her home, a police official told AFP on Monday.

Japan has the second-oldest population in the world after Monaco, and senior citizens are often targeted by fraudsters, who last year collectively stole around 325.7 billion yen ($2.0 billion) from their victims.
The woman, who lives in the Shiga region, received telephone calls from Wednesday through Thursday last week from a man who claimed to be a police officer.
The caller falsely informed her that her bank account had experienced an unauthorized withdrawal.
The woman was told to give her ATM card to a man, posing as a police officer, who would visit her so authorities could verify her account.
Suspecting a scam, the woman consulted her son and the police as she waited for the man to visit her house.

"The person's family reached out to the police on Wednesday evening, and we were able to have officers at her house" before the scammer arrived on Thursday, a local police official told AFP on the customary condition of anonymity.
When a 47-year-old man appeared at her doorstep, waiting officers arrested him on the spot, the police official said.
"The person (the woman) is someone in good health and highly articulate," the official said, while urging other elderly residents to consult family members when they suspect fraud.

一名警官周一告诉法新社，日本西部一名 93 岁的妇女假装上当，并帮助警方在她家中逮​​捕一名诈骗嫌疑人，从而智胜了一名诈骗嫌疑人。
日本是世界上人口第二多的国家，仅次于摩纳哥，老年人经常成为诈骗者的目标，去年诈骗者总共从受害者那里窃取了约 3,257 亿日元（20 亿美元）。
这名住在滋贺地区的妇女上周周三至周四接到了一名自称是警察的男子打来的电话。
来电者谎称她的银行账户遭到未经授权的提款。
该女子被告知将她的 ATM 卡交给一名冒充警察的男子，该男子会拜访她，以便当局核实她的账户。
由于怀疑遭到诈骗，该女子在等待该男子到她家拜访时咨询了她的儿子和警方。
当地一名不愿透露姓名的警方官员告诉法新社，“周三晚上，该人的家人联系了警方，在骗子周四到达之前，我们已经派警察到她家了”。
这名警官说，当一名 47 岁的男子出现在她家门口时，等待的警察当场逮捕了他。
这位官员表示，“此人（该女子）身体健康，口才很好”，同时敦促其他老年居民在怀疑有欺诈行为时咨询家人。
