title_en: NFL Week 7: A divisional duel in Detroit, and Aaron Rodgers keeps winning
title_zh: NFL 第 7 周：底特律分区对决，亚伦·罗杰斯持续获胜
summary: Week 7 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl contender getting back on track and a thrilling divisional showdown in the NFC North, plus another comeback win for one of the NFL’s most surprising teams.
summary_zh: NFL 赛季第 7 周，超级碗竞争者重回正轨，并在 NFC 北部地区展开一场激动人心的分区对决，此外还有另一场比赛
body_en: Week 7 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl contender getting back on track and a thrilling divisional showdown in the NFC North, plus another comeback win for one of the NFL’s most surprising teams.
Here’s what you need to know about from Sunday.

What a game between the Detroit Lions and the Green Bay Packers in the late window. The Lions won 20-17 on a walk-off field goal after a drama-filled affair that included controversial calls, plenty of offense and even an offensive lineman running a drag route.

Both quarterbacks were dealing. Detroit’s Jared Goff completed 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards in the win, while Green Bay’s Jordan Love was 22 of 32 for 303 yards. Love could have had an even bigger day, but his receivers had multiple drops in big moments.

The game was also filled with miscues. The Packers missed two field goals, both of which were shorter than 40 yards. Detroit, meanwhile, had two turnovers after not having given the ball away even once since Week 1.
The fourth quarter was especially intense. The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 24 but were stuffed on a run.
Green Bay couldn’t take advantage on its ensuing possession, however. After they picked up only 5 yards, the Packers lined up for a 35-yard field goal, but Trey Smack’s kick was deflected.
Detroit’s offense finally finished the job from there, going 71 yards and running out the clock for a game-winning kick by Jake Bates. The Lions improved to 4-2, while the Packers fell to 4-3.
Cleveland improved to 5-2 after a last-minute, 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans.

The Browns are not only one of the NFL’s most surprising teams; they are the league’s comeback kings so far this season. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has led a game-winning drive in each of the team’s five wins this year, and those five game-winning drives are the most by any Cleveland quarterback in a single season this century, per ESPN.

The Browns got a breakout game from rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion, who had eight catches for 129 yards. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr. made a huge play late with a 36-yard catch and run to set up a game-winning field goal.

Can Cleveland keep this up? All five of its wins have come by four points or less. The Browns have a negative-13 point differential despite their winning record. Cleveland keeps winning, but the margins are super thin.
J.J. McCarthy gets his first win for the Giants
A week after he threw 243 yards in relief of Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy got the start for New York and led the Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans in overtime.

McCarthy played a clean game, completing 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. He improved to 7-4 in his career as a starter, and New York is now 4-2-1 — and atop the NFC East. McCarthy got a huge boost from his rushing attack, as Cam Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a score, while former Texan Devin Singletary ran for the winning touchdown in the extra period.

It’s been a frustrating season for Los Angeles, which entered Week 7 with a 2-4 record. The Rams’ last three losses came by a combined nine points, a sign the team was closer to the preseason favorite most assumed it would be.

Los Angeles finally lived up to its potential in a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The Rams scored 28 points in the first half alone, thanks in large part to a rushing attack that averaged 5.2 yards per rush en route to 199 yards. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford was efficient, finishing the game with 195 yards on 23 of 29 passing.
Los Angeles’ next three games are against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Washington Commanders and the Arizona Cardinals — an opportunity for the 3-4 Rams to get back over .500.

After quarterback Aaron Rodgers looked every bit his age in a sluggish start to the season, the 42-year-old four-time MVP has led Pittsburgh to a 4-1 record in its last five games. The Steelers squeaked out a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris in a game played without incident amid protests in France.

Rodgers has completed at least 60% of his passes in each of the last three weeks, all of which were Pittsburgh wins. On Sunday, he even dialed back the clock to pick up a key first down late with his legs, effectively icing the game.
body_zh: NFL 赛季第七周，超级碗竞争者重回正轨，并在 NFC 北部地区展开一场激动人心的分区对决，此外，NFL 最令人惊讶的球队之一又卷土重来取得胜利。
以下是您从周日起需要了解的信息。
底特律雄狮队和绿湾包装工队在窗口期末的比赛真是一场精彩的比赛。在一场充满戏剧性的事件之后，狮子队以 20-17 的远距离射门获胜，其中包括有争议的判罚、大量的进攻，甚至还有一名进攻线卫在拖拽路线。
两名四分卫都在发球。底特律队的贾里德·戈夫在这场胜利中45次传球完成27次，推进274码，而绿湾队的乔丹·乐福则32次传球完成22次，推进303码。乐福本来可以拥有更伟大的一天，但他的接球手在重要时刻多次掉球。
这场比赛也充满了失误。包装工队两次投丢球，距离均小于 40 码。与此同时，底特律自第一周以来就没有丢过一次球，因此出现了两次失误。
第四节比赛尤其激烈。雄狮队在自己的 24 场比赛中以第四场和第一场的成绩取得了胜利，但在跑动中陷入了困境。
然而，绿湾队无法利用随后的控球优势。在他们只推进了 5 码后，包装工队准备进行 35 码的射门，但特雷·斯马克的射门被挡住。
底特律的进攻终于从这里完成了任务，在时间紧迫的情况下，杰克·贝茨 (Jake Bates) 射出了 71 码，赢得了比赛。雄狮队将战绩提高到4胜2负，而包装工队则跌至4胜3负。
克利夫兰在最后时刻以27-24战胜田纳西泰坦队，战绩升至5胜2负。
布朗队不仅是 NFL 中最令人惊讶的球队之一，也是 NFL 中最令人惊讶的球队之一。他们是本赛季迄今为止联盟的复出之王。据 ESPN 报道，四分卫德肖恩·沃森 (Deshaun Watson) 在今年球队的五场胜利中，每场都带领球队致胜，而这五次致胜进攻是本世纪克利夫兰四分卫中单赛季最多的。
布朗队在新秀外接手 KC Concepcion 的帮助下取得了突破，他接球 8 次，推进 129 码。近端锋小哈罗德·范宁 (Harold Fannin Jr.) 在比赛最后时刻表现出色，接球后跑出 36 码，射入制胜进球。
克利夫兰能保持这样的势头吗？所有五场胜利的得分都在 4 分或更少。尽管布朗队取得了胜利，但他们仍落后 13 分。克利夫兰持续获胜，但利润微薄。
J.J.麦卡锡为巨人队赢得了第一场胜利
一周后，他接替杰梅斯·温斯顿 (Jameis Winston) 投出 243 码，J.J.麦卡锡为纽约队首发，带领巨人队在加时赛中以27-21战胜休斯敦德州人队。
麦卡锡的比赛干净利落，28次传球完成20次，推进252码。作为先发球员，他的职业生涯战绩提高到了 7 胜 4 负，而纽约现在的战绩是 4 胜 2 平 1 负，位居国联东部榜首。麦卡锡的冲球进攻给麦卡锡带来了巨大的推动力，卡姆·斯卡特博跑出了 124 码并得分，而前德克萨斯人德文·辛格特里则在加时赛中取得了制胜达阵。
对于洛杉矶来说，这是一个令人沮丧的赛季，他们以 2 胜 4 负的战绩进入第七周。公羊队过去三场失利的总分是九分，这表明球队更接近季前赛最热门的球队。
洛杉矶最终发挥了自己的潜力，以 35-21 击败拉斯维加斯突袭者队。公羊队仅在上半场就拿下了 28 分，这在很大程度上要归功于冲球进攻，平均每次冲球距离为 5.2 码，最终冲球距离达到 199 码。卫冕 MVP 马修·斯塔福德表现高效，全场 29 次传球 23 码，推进 195 码。
洛杉矶队接下来的三场比赛将对阵洛杉矶闪电队、华盛顿指挥官队和亚利桑那红雀队，这是 3-4 公羊队扳回 0.500 以上的机会。
四分卫亚伦·罗杰斯在赛季开局表现不佳，看起来完全不像他的年龄，这位 42 岁的四届 MVP 在过去的五场比赛中带领匹兹堡队取得了 4 胜 1 负的战绩。钢人队在巴黎以 16-10 战胜新奥尔良圣徒队，这场比赛在法国的抗议活动中没有发生任何事件。
罗杰斯在过去三周的每一周都完成了至少 60% 的传球，所有这些都是匹兹堡的胜利。周日，他甚至拨回了时间，用双腿率先拿起了钥匙，有效地为比赛降温。

title_en: Campaigns drag grieving families into midterm attack ads
title_zh: 活动将悲伤的家庭拖入中期攻击广告
summary: The 2026 midterms have taken a deeply personal turn as campaigns use other people's family tragedies as political ammunition — sometimes over the objections of the families themselves. Why it matters: Some attack ads feature photographs of murdered children an
summary_zh: 2026 年中期选举发生了深刻的个人转变，竞选活动利用他人的家庭悲剧作为政治弹药——有时甚至超越了目标。
body_en: The 2026 midterms have taken a deeply personal turn as campaigns use other people's family tragedies as political ammunition — sometimes over the objections of the families themselves.
Why it matters: Some attack ads feature photographs of murdered children and anguished 911 calls, forcing grieving families to relive their worst moments.

Georgia governor race: Republican gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson used images of murdered 8-year-old Secoriea Turner and her mother's anguished 911 call to attack Democratic rival Keisha Lance Bottoms, Atlanta's former mayor.
Turner's family demanded the ads come down, accusing the campaign of exploiting their grief without permission. Jackson said he would keep airing them .
Ohio governor race: Ohio Republican gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign is spending $4 million on an ad featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton.
In the ad, Donna Arthur calls her daughter a liar and disputes her account of childhood homelessness.

Acton says her late stepfather — who was married to her mother until his death — sexually abused her as a child, and she hasn't spoken to her mother in decades. Acton's brother corroborated her account , while court records and contemporary news reports support key details.
President Trump urged Ramaswamy to keep running his attack on Acton, despite objections from some fellow Republicans.
Between the lines: Ramaswamy's campaign said the ad tested well with persuadable voters , even as critics warned it could backfire.

Ohio Senate race: A Republican attack ad against former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown featured images of a couple and their 1-year-old son killed in a highway crash to blame Brown's immigration policies.
The victims' family demanded its removal , saying nobody sought permission to use their relatives' images or tragedy.
North Carolina Senate race: A Republican super PAC featured a grieving father in an attack ad linking the murder of his 23-year-old son to former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper's prison policies.
The father said he felt deceived about the ad's purpose. The group disputes his account, while fact-checkers found no connection between the killer and Cooper's prisoner-release agreement.
Yes, but: Some survivors willingly share their trauma to challenge politicians' decisions.
In Nebraska, Jody Snogren voluntarily appeared in an ad attacking Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts for his 2022 vote to pardon John Arias, who pleaded guilty to raping her.
Snogren told The 19th she chose to tell her story to inform voters and had no regrets.
Ricketts expressed sympathy for Snogren but defended the pardon , noting Arias had served his full sentence and the pardon came decades after the crime.
body_zh: 2026 年中期选举发生了深刻的个人转变，竞选活动利用他人的家庭悲剧作为政治弹药——有时甚至不顾家庭本身的反对。
重要性：一些攻击性广告展示了被谋杀儿童的照片和痛苦的 911 电话，迫使悲伤的家庭重温他们最糟糕的时刻。
佐治亚州州长竞选：共和党州长候选人里克·杰克逊 (Rick Jackson) 使用被谋杀的 8 岁女孩塞科里亚·特纳 (Secoriea Turner) 和她母亲痛苦的 911 电话的照片来攻击民主党竞争对手、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms)。
特纳的家人要求撤下这些广告，指责该活动未经许可利用了他们的悲伤。杰克逊表示他会继续播放它们。
俄亥俄州州长竞选：俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米(Vivek Ramaswamy)的竞选团队斥资400万美元制作一则广告，主角是民主党对手艾米·阿克顿(Amy Acton)关系疏远的母亲。
在广告中，唐娜·阿瑟称她的女儿是个骗子，并对她关于童年无家可归的说法提出异议。
阿克顿说，她已故的继父——他在她母亲去世前一直与她结婚——在她小时候对她进行了性虐待，她已经几十年没有和她的母亲说过话了。阿克顿的兄弟证实了她的说法，而法庭记录和当代新闻报道则支持了关键细节。
尽管一些共和党同僚反对，特朗普总统仍敦促拉马斯瓦米继续攻击阿克顿。
言外之意是：拉马斯瓦米的竞选团队表示，该广告在有说服力的选民中效果良好，尽管批评者警告称这可能会适得其反。
俄亥俄州参议员竞选：共和党针对前民主党参议员谢罗德·布朗的攻击广告中出现了一对夫妇和他们一岁的儿子在高速公路车祸中丧生的照片，以此指责布朗的移民政策。
受害者家属要求将其移除，称没有人寻求许可使用其亲属的照片或悲剧。
北卡罗来纳州参议院竞选：共和党超级政治行动委员会在一则攻击性广告中以一位悲伤的父亲为主角，将他 23 岁儿子的谋杀案与前民主党州长罗伊·库珀的监狱政策联系起来。
父亲说他觉得广告的目的受到了欺骗。该组织对他的说法提出质疑，而事实核查人员发现凶手与库珀的囚犯释放协议之间没有任何联系。
是的，但是：一些幸存者愿意分享他们的创伤来挑战政客的决定。
在内布拉斯加州，乔迪·斯诺格伦 (Jody Snogren) 自愿出现在一则广告中，攻击共和党参议员皮特·里基茨 (Pete Ricketts) 2022 年投票赦免约翰·阿里亚斯 (John Arias)，后者承认强奸了她。
斯诺格伦告诉《十九号报》，她选择讲述自己的故事是为了让选民知道，并且并不后悔。
里基茨对斯诺格伦表示同情，但为赦免辩护，指出阿里亚斯已服满刑期，赦免是在犯罪发生几十年后发生的。

title_en: Special ed diaries: Teachers tell NPR about their most joyous, most difficult moments
title_zh: 特别编辑日记：老师们向 NPR 讲述他们最快乐、最困难的时刻
summary: What makes special education teaching jobs so hard to fill? NPR set out to find some answers by talking to more than a dozen teachers who do this work every day.
summary_zh: 是什么让特殊教育教学职位如此难以填补？ NPR 开始通过与十几位从事这项工作的老师交谈来寻找一些答案
body_en: Special ed diaries: Teachers tell NPR about their most joyous, most difficult moments

Top row (from left): Danalyn Garcia of Chicago Public Schools, Lucie Lane of Shawnee Mission School District in Kansas, Jeff Carroll of Newport News Public Schools in Virginia and Kaori Anderson-Walker of Boys' Latin of Philadelphia Charter School.

Bottom row (from left): Paul Stone of Mt. Diablo Unified School District in California, Diana Swanson of Vail School District in Arizona, Kathleen Tejeda of Alvord Unified School District in California and Emily Ellis of Lexington School District Two in South Carolina. LA Johnson/NPR hide caption
One of Kathleen Tejeda's students began freshman year just trying to get by. High school can be tricky for any teenager, but she was navigating it as a blind person.

By the end of her junior year, with support from Tejeda and other school staff, the student had gone from getting by to going big: She made the cheerleading squad and the school choir. She even sang the national anthem in front of the whole school.

Tejeda, who has been a special educator for 20 years in Riverside County, Calif., said that kind of advocacy is just as much a part of her job as teaching her students. But teachers like her can be hard to find.

There is a shortage of special educators in 45 out of 50 states , according to the Learning Policy Institute, an education research organization. That shortage is growing because the number of special education students is climbing: It's now more than 8.2 million — about 1 out of 6 public school students.

While turnover worsened sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic, the shortage isn't new. It has existed since special education became embedded in federal law with the passage of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act in 1975. Half a century later, a fundamental question remains: Why is this shortage of special education teachers so persistent?
Myths and realities about teaching special education

Let's start with a common misconception: The kids are hard to work with, so teachers don't want to do the job. "That is not the case," said Liz Bettini, a former special education teacher who is now a researcher and professor at Boston University. "That has not borne out in our research at all."

What Bettini's research does show: Special educators can feel isolated from other school staff and feel they have too many student needs to manage. The volume of required paperwork can be crushing. These educators are often responsible for teaching across several subjects and grade levels. Many feel they don't get paid enough to do this essential work.
"That's a very heavy weight to carry as a teacher," Bettini said.

NPR set out to hear directly from about a dozen special educators from around the United States' public schools to learn what it takes to do their jobs day to day. They have been sharing snippets of their lives through voice memos since the start of the school year, and some will open their classroom doors to NPR in the coming months.

"No teacher does this for the paycheck," said third-year high school teacher Diana Swanson, who works in Vail, Ariz., as she sat at her desk the day before her school year began in July. "Just the students, that fulfillment, seeing them fill their cup a little bit, seeing them smile, be a member of society and part of their community. That's what fulfills me."
Overworked and understaffed: Special ed teachers turn to AI for help

"I feel like I was coming into this school year more prepared this time around," fourth-year elementary school teacher Danalyn Garcia said late one school night from her living room in Chicago. "Yet, I feel the needs are even greater than the year before."

"Honestly, I had no life outside of school and outside of being a teacher," said Kaori Anderson-Walker, looking back on his first year of teaching middle school in Philadelphia. Now in his fourth year, he said he has finally learned to manage his time more effectively but said the work is still never-ending. "When my students aren't performing where I want them in the classroom, my mind is just constantly moving."

Being an educator of any kind is demanding and requires immense skill. Research shows that burnout among all kinds of public school teachers is high, but it's even more acute for special educators. These teachers work with students who have an incredibly diverse set of needs, including those with autism, learning disabilities such as dyslexia, developmental delays and physical disabilities.

Special educators also do a lot more than teach — in fact, one study found that they spent only about a third of their day on instruction. They spend the rest of their time tracking student goals, coordinating specialized services for students (say, speech therapy or extra reading help), training support staff and writing individualized education programs (IEPs), which are legal documents that track each special education student's needs at school.

In many states, that means teachers must have specialized certification and training, but they typically aren't paid more. In 32 states, teachers get no extra pay for the hardest-to-staff positions, including in special education, according to a recent study .
body_zh: 特别编辑日记：老师们向 NPR 讲述他们最快乐、最困难的时刻
顶排（左起）：芝加哥公立学校的 Danalyn Garcia、堪萨斯州肖尼教会学区的 Lucie Lane、弗吉尼亚州纽波特纽斯公立学校的 Jeff Carroll 和费城特许学校男子拉丁学校的 Kaori Anderson-Walker。
下排（左起）：加利福尼亚州迪亚波罗山联合学区的保罗·斯通、亚利桑那州韦尔学区的戴安娜·斯旺森、加利福尼亚州阿尔沃德联合学区的凯瑟琳·特赫达和南卡罗来纳州列克星敦第二学区的艾米丽·埃利斯。洛杉矶约翰逊/NPR 隐藏标题栏
凯瑟琳·特赫达（Kathleen Tejeda）的一名学生刚开始一年级时只是想勉强度日。高中对于任何青少年来说都是很棘手的，但她却以盲人的身份度过了这一切。
到了大三结束时，在特赫达和其他学校工作人员的支持下，这位学生已经从勉强过关变成了大人：她加入了啦啦队和学校合唱团。她甚至在全校面前唱国歌。
特赫达在加利福尼亚州里弗赛德县担任了 20 年的特殊教育工作者，她说这种宣传与教育学生一样是她工作的一部分。但像她这样的老师很难找到。
根据教育研究组织学习政策研究所的数据，50 个州中有 45 个州缺乏特殊教育工作者。由于特殊教育学生人数不断攀升，这种短缺现象日益严重：目前已超过 820 万人——约占公立学校学生的六分之一。
尽管 COVID-19 大流行后营业额急剧恶化，但短缺现象并不新鲜。自从 1975 年《残疾人教育法案》通过，特殊教育被纳入联邦法律以来，这种现象就一直存在。半个世纪后，一个基本问题仍然存在：为什么特殊教育教师的短缺如此持续？
关于特殊教育教学的神话和现实
让我们从一个常见的误解开始：孩子们很难相处，所以老师不想做这项工作。 “事实并非如此，”前特殊教育教师、现波士顿大学研究员兼教授利兹·贝蒂尼 (Liz Bettini) 说。 “我们的研究根本没有证实这一点。”
贝蒂尼的研究确实表明：特殊教育工作者可能会感到与其他学校工作人员孤立，并感觉他们有太多的学生需求需要管理。所需的文书工作量可能非常巨大。这些教育工作者通常负责多个学科和年级的教学。许多人觉得他们没有得到足够的报酬来完成这项重要的工作。
“作为一名教师，这是一个非常沉重的负担，”贝蒂尼说。
NPR 开始直接听取来自美国各地公立学校的大约十几名特殊教育工作者的意见，了解如何完成他们的日常工作。自学年开始以来，他们一直通过语音备忘录分享生活片段，有些人将在未来几个月内向 NPR 打开课堂大门。
在亚利桑那州韦尔工作的三年级高中教师戴安娜·斯旺森 (Diana Swanson) 在 7 月份学年开始的前一天坐在办公桌前说道：“没有老师为了薪水而这样做。” “只有学生，那种满足感，看到他们倒满杯子，看到他们微笑，成为社会的一员，成为社区的一部分。这就是我的满足感。”
过度劳累和人手不足：特殊教育教师向人工智能寻求帮助
“我觉得这次我在进入新学年时准备得更加充分，”四年级小学教师达纳琳·加西亚在芝加哥的一个学校深夜在她的客厅里说道。 “然而，我觉得需求比前一年还要大。”
“老实说，除了学校和当老师之外，我没有什么生活，”Kaori Anderson-Walker 在回顾他在费城教中学的第一年时说道。现在已经是第四年了，他说他终于学会了更有效地管理自己的时间，但他说工作仍然永无止境。 “当我的学生在课堂上没有达到我想要的表现时，我的思绪就会不断变化。”
成为任何类型的教育者都要求很高，需要极高的技能。研究表明，各类公立学校教师的职业倦怠程度都很高，但特殊教育工作者的职业倦怠程度更为严重。这些老师与有着极其多样化需求的学生一起工作，包括患有自闭症、阅读障碍等学习障碍、发育迟缓和身体残疾的学生。
特殊教育工作者所做的不仅仅是教学——事实上，一项研究发现，他们每天只花大约三分之一的时间在教学上。他们把剩下的时间花在跟踪学生目标、协调为学生提供的专业服务（例如言语治疗或额外阅读帮助）、培训支持人员以及编写个性化教育计划 (IEP)，这是跟踪每个特殊教育学生在学校需求的法律文件。
在许多州，这意味着教师必须拥有专门的认证和培训，但他们的薪水通常不会更高。根据最近的一项研究，在 32 个州，教师对于最难担任的职位（包括特殊教育部门）没有额外报酬。

title_en: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts
title_zh: 人工智能如何改变飓风预测
summary: Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions.
summary_zh: 飓风预报员越来越多地使用人工智能进行预测。
body_en: A satellite image provided by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) shows Hurricane Isaias approaching the Gulf Coast of Alabama and Florida on Friday, Oct. 9 2026. NOAA/NOAA hide caption
Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions — and they say the technology is rapidly transforming the field.
When the first hurricane of the Atlantic season formed this month, an AI model beat out traditional models at predicting where it would go.
The Pacific is churning with hurricanes. The Atlantic is quiet. Blame El Niño

In early October, Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., as a Category 2 storm. Conventional forecasting models initially predicted it would head further west, toward southeastern Louisiana.
But Google DeepMind's artificial intelligence model called it right out of the gate: the hurricane was going to hit the western Florida Panhandle.

"Google DeepMind, in particular, has really proven itself the last few years as the gold standard model," says Michael Lowry, a longtime meteorologist and hurricane expert in Miami, who has previously advised both the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the National Hurricane Center (NHC).
"That model has been, by far and away, the best performing computer model that we've ever seen. Period."
The National Hurricane Center first started incorporating the Google DeepMind model into its official forecasts last year.
As the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season ends, the future of forecasting is AI
By the end of the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, it was already one of the best at predicting a storm's path and strength, says Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher for the University of Miami.
Usually, new models take years to refine after first being introduced.

"It's something we're not used to – to have a model, the new kid on the block, very quickly becoming the best model out there," McNoldy says. "This pretty much came out of the gate in first place, and that's a pretty impressive feat."

Traditional physics-based hurricane models use real-time atmospheric data, like temperature, humidity, pressure and wind shear, as measured by satellites and aircraft. Then they use complicated equations to predict what path a storm might travel and how strong it could get.
An AI model operates very differently: it relies more on history. It identifies patterns by analyzing thousands of past storms along with atmospheric data.

"The AI models don't really know anything about the atmosphere other than the current picture," Lowry says. "Beyond that, it's not leaning on the governing equations of the atmosphere, the physics, to make predictions."
United Nations report highlights significant increase in U.S. climate pollution
Most of the people designing and developing these models aren't even meteorologists, Lowry notes: "They're software engineers, and they're developing neural networks."
A "neural network" is a set of computer algorithms modeled on the human brain and trained to find patterns in massive amounts of data.
As a result, the models can seem like a "black box," Lowry says: "We don't know why they might get a forecast right. We also don't know why they might get a forecast wrong."

飓风预报员越来越多地使用人工智能进行预测，他们表示这项技术正在迅速改变这个领域。
当大西洋季节的第一场飓风本月形成时，人工智能模型在预测飓风去向方面击败了传统模型。
太平洋正遭受飓风袭击。大西洋很平静。归咎于厄尔尼诺现象
10 月初，飓风伊萨亚斯在佛罗里达州德斯坦附近登陆，为 2 级风暴。传统的预测模型最初预测它将进一步向西，向路易斯安那州东南部移动。
但谷歌 DeepMind 的人工智能模型一开始就预测：飓风将袭击佛罗里达州西部狭长地带。
“尤其是 Google DeepMind，在过去几年中确实证明了自己是黄金标准模型，”迈阿密的长期气象学家和飓风专家 Michael Lowry 说，他之前曾为联邦紧急事务管理局和国家飓风中心 (NHC) 提供咨询。
“迄今为止，该模型是我们见过的性能最好的计算机模型。就这样。”
美国国家飓风中心去年首次开始将谷歌 DeepMind 模型纳入其官方预测中。
随着 2025 年大西洋飓风季节结束，预测的未来是人工智能
迈阿密大学飓风研​​究员布莱恩·麦克诺迪 (Brian McNoldy) 表示，到 2025 年大西洋飓风季节结束时，它已经成为预测风暴路径和强度的最佳工具之一。
通常，新模型在首次推出后需要数年时间来完善。
“这是我们不习惯的事情——拥有一个模特，这个街区的新人，很快就成为最好的模特，”麦克诺迪说。 “这几乎是一开始就出现的，这是一个非常令人印象深刻的壮举。”
传统的基于物理的飓风模型使用卫星和飞机测量的实时大气数据，例如温度、湿度、压力和风切变。然后，他们使用复杂的方程来预测风暴可能行进的路径以及风暴的强度。
人工智能模型的运作方式非常不同：它更多地依赖于历史。它通过分析过去数千次风暴以及大气数据来识别模式。
“除了当前图片之外，人工智能模型并不真正了解有关大气的任何信息，”洛瑞说。 “除此之外，它并不依赖大气、物理学的控制方程来做出预测。”
联合国报告强调美国气候污染显着增加
洛瑞指出，大多数设计和开发这些模型的人甚至都不是气象学家：“他们是软件工程师，他们正在开发神经网络。”
“神经网络”是一组模仿人脑的计算机算法，经过训练可以在大量数据中查找模式。
因此，这些模型看起来就像一个“黑匣子”，洛瑞说：“我们不知道为什么他们可能会做出正确的预测。我们也不知道为什么他们可能会做出错误的预测。”
